title: Chris Van Hollen to run for US Senate majority leader
excerpt: US Senator Chris Van Hollen has said he is running for Senate majority leader as Democrats gear up to take charge of the US Congress in January following a Democratic landslide in this month’s midterm...
body_text:
US Senator Chris Van Hollen has said he is running for Senate majority leader as Democrats gear up to take charge of the US Congress in January following a Democratic landslide in this month’s midterm elections.

Van Hollen said in a post on X late on Thursday that Americans had “called on us to unrig an economy rigged against working people & fueled by political corruption”.

“To deliver, we need new leadership,” he said, adding that “this isn’t about any one person – it’s about answering that call”.

Van Hollen has faced mounting calls to enter the race for Senate majority leader amid growing opposition to Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer‘s continued tenure after he faced criticism over how he has handled the Democratic caucus during the Trump presidency.

US Senator-elect Abdul El-Sayed from Michigan was the first to back Van Hollen’s decision to run. In a post on X, El-Sayed said: “I called on Sen. Chris Van Hollen to lead our caucus as a candidate back in April because he leads with courage and experience.”

“We need both right now. Which is why I’m proud to stand with him in his bid to lead our Senate majority,” El-Sayed said.

On Thursday, Democratic Party leaders gathered in Denver, Colorado, for a two-day conference on the future of the party, following the sweeping victories in the midterms.

Some progressives at the conference have argued that it is time to change the direction and the leadership of the Democratic Party.

“[Chuck] Schumer has spent nearly 50 years in elected office,” said Washington, DC-based political commentator and strategist James Butler, adding that while he respected the US senator’s service, “it is time for veteran Democrats to make space for younger, more energetic members”.

Senator Chris Van Hollen of Maryland has repeatedly challenged Washington’s relationship with Middle Eastern partners.

Van Hollen, the son of a US diplomat, has called Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu a “chronic liar“, previously telling Al Jazeera the US-Israel war on Iran “is making America and our allies less safe”.

He also attempted to push forward legislation in Congress that would have required the Trump administration to report on the killing of nine Americans in the occupied West Bank and on Israel’s treatment of Palestinian children in military detention.

This week, Van Hollen and 10 Senate colleagues urged congressional leaders to remove provisions from the annual defence policy bill that would expand weapons development and intelligence sharing with Israel.

title: Toronto Blue Jays apologize after Muslim community outcry over Anthony Santander's Instagram posts
excerpt: Fans always beg college football coaches to stop giving boring, robotic press conference answers—and ahead of Saturday's showdown in Eugene, these two delivered pure fireworks while pretending they "r...
body_text:
Fans always beg college football coaches to stop giving boring, robotic press conference answers—and ahead of Saturday's showdown in Eugene, these two delivered pure fireworks while pretending they "respect" each other.

The Toronto Blue Jays issued a corporate apology Thursday after activist groups targeted outfielder Anthony Santander over political Instagram posts he shared last week.

Caving to activist pressure, the team met with local Muslim leaders before president and CEO Mark Shapiro issued the following statement.

Anthony Santander and Vladimir Guerrero Jr. of the Toronto Blue Jays celebrate after Guerrero hit a home run during the fifth inning against the Seattle Mariners in Game 3 of the American League Championship Series at T-Mobile Park on Oct. 15, 2025, in Seattle, Wash. (Getty Images)

"We met with leaders in Toronto's Muslim communities today, who shared the harm caused by Anthony Santander's Islamophobic social media posts. The opportunity to listen and learn was important and reaffirms our beliefs and values as an organization. We condemn Islamophobia and all forms of hate.

REGGIE JACKSON CALLS OUT ANTISEMITISM IN NATIVE PENNSYLVANIA, LIKENS IT TO 'RACISM I EXPERIENCED IN THE 1960S'

"The Blue Jays are deeply sorry to the Muslim community and our fans for the pain and harm these Islamophobic posts have caused. We will work with leaders in Muslim communities to fight against all forms of hate. The Blue Jays will continue to ensure our organization reflects the inclusive community we are proud to call home."

Santander ruffled some feathers last week after progressive Democrat Abdul El-Sayed won Michigan's U.S. Senate race.

Anthony Santander #25 of the Toronto Blue Jays takes the field during Game One of the American League Championship Series between the Seattle Mariners and the Toronto Blue Jays at Rogers Centre on Sunday, Oct. 12, 2025, in Toronto, Ontario, Canada. (MLB Photos via Getty Images)

A native of Venezuela who grew up under socialist rule, Santander shared third-party Instagram stories, which included a thumbnail of El-Sayed reading "America voted for Sharia last night," a graphic stating, "Islam is not peaceful," and a preacher claiming, "there is no such thing as kind Muslims."

Santander deleted the posts two days later.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

Advocacy groups and online critics condemned the posts, demanding the franchise cancel the outfielder. Steven Zhou of the National Council of Canadian Muslims told reporters that community members were "very, very upset."

Anthony Santander #25 of the Toronto Blue Jays takes the field before Game 3 of the American League Championship Series between the Toronto Blue Jays and the Seattle Mariners at T-Mobile Park on Wednesday, Oct. 15, 2025, in Seattle, Wash. (MLB Photos via Getty Images)

Zhou attended Thursday's meeting and reported the club committed to putting Santander through educational training, though Shapiro's statement mentioned no discipline.

Despite the pressure, Santander has not apologized or commented publicly.

Speaking Tuesday at MLB's general manager meetings, Blue Jays GM Ross Atkins said there were no words to express his disappointment and confirmed he told Santander he needed to address the situation.

MLB COMMISSIONER TELLS SEN. HAWLEY GIANTS PLAYERS WON’T BE DISCIPLINED OVER BIBLE VERSES ON PRIDE NIGHT HATS

Neither the Blue Jays nor Major League Baseball has announced a fine, suspension or roster move, and it mostly comes down to payroll.

Cutting Santander would force Toronto to absorb $49 million in remaining guaranteed money.

Since signing in 2025, Santander has played in just 54 games, missing the entire 2026 season after shoulder surgery.

For now, the Blue Jays are willing to issue apologies to appease activists.

Send us your thoughts: alejandro.avila@outkick.com / Follow along on X: @alejandroaveela

Alejandro Avila is a longtime writer at OutKick, living in Southern California.

title: Scandal-hit Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang quits, plunging AI chipmaking giant into turmoil
excerpt:
How could the Nvidia CEO’s affair threaten US national security?

Jensen Huang has abruptly quit as chief executive of AI chipmaking giant Nvidia after revelations of alleged extramarital affairs, in ...
body_text:
How could the Nvidia CEO’s affair threaten US national security?

Jensen Huang has abruptly quit as chief executive of AI chipmaking giant Nvidia after revelations of alleged extramarital affairs, in a stunning fall from grace that sent shockwaves from Silicon Valley to Capitol Hill.

Nvidia is now under scrutiny from US lawmakers in Washington DC demanding Huang answer questions over whether one of his alleged relationships was with a Chinese spy.

One of the world's most valuable companies as a result of the AI boom, Nvidia has lost $550bn (£415bn) in stock market value in just five days as the scandal dominated headlines.

Nvidia's interim CEO, Colette Kress, called an emergency meeting of her executive team to discuss the company's future.

His alleged conduct not only potentially crossed professional boundaries, but has made Nvidia the target of questions from US politicians who have expressed concern about national security risks.

Huang, who has been Nvidia's public face since 1993, admitted on Sunday to having been "unfaithful" to his wife after reports he had an affair with a suspected Chinese spy, Alice Huang.

On Wednesday, he was reported to have had a second relationship, this time with an Nvidia executive.

Alice Huang (no relation) worked as an executive at the Singaporean firm Megaspeed. She has been suspected of being an intelligence asset for China, according to the New York Times. China has rejected that allegation as a smear.

Watch: What we know so far about Nvidia CEO resignation

And US Attorney General Todd Blanche said on Thursday the Department of Justice had not yet drawn any conclusions about whether Alice Huang was engaged in espionage for Beijing.

Senators Elizabeth Warren and Chris Coons, along with other Democrats on the House Foreign Affairs Committee, publicly demanded that Huang brief Congress on the matter.

If he refuses to appear voluntarily before any committee that calls him, he could be subpoenaed, one Senate staff member told the BBC.

Nvidia officials have repeatedly declined to comment since Wednesday. A personal representative of Huang also declined to comment on Thursday.

According to US media, Huang's alleged second affair was with a long-time Nvidia executive, Kimberly Powell, who reported directly to him within the company.

Sources have told the BBC that Nvidia employees had noticed the pair were unusually close.

Huang had been widely expected to weather the storm after the first affair became public, even as Nvidia announced it had launched an investigation into whether its CEO had been "the target of a foreign intelligence effort".

One current Nvidia staff member told the BBC that the initial reports of his infidelity were more or less brushed off by rank-and-file workers inside the company.

It wasn't until Huang's alleged affair with the Nvidia executive became public that workers started to feel "this is crazy", the person said.

Another Nvidia employee said they had been told not to speak with the press or otherwise comment on the situation in public.

Many staff have earned millions of dollars in compensation through their ability to cash out their Nvidia shares as the stock soared.

Nvidia has said it has "no reason to believe that either national security or Nvidia secrets were compromised", but pledged that its independent inquiry would look at all available information.

The company's meteoric rise had been led by Jensen Huang, who became a major booster of the AI industry, which relies on Nvidia for the powerful computer chips it manufactures.

Initially those chips were designed for computer gaming.

But as AI technology evolved in the last four years into chatbots and large language models, companies building AI tools suddenly required huge numbers of the Nvidia computer chips that could process large amounts of data.

Nvidia is now hunting a permanent replacement for Huang. Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress was named on Thursday as interim CEO.

Several tech insiders that the BBC spoke with this week noted that Huang's downfall has been a major topic of conversation in San Francisco Bay area circles, an area filled with tech employees, industry executives and billionaires.

He is far from the first tech titan to become embroiled in revelations of infidelity.

Bill Gates of Microsoft and Jeff Bezos of Amazon had affairs exposed in the last decade. Both men are now divorced from their wives.

Huang has been married to Lori Huang for 40 years. Both of their children are also executives at Nvidia.

Nvidia's stock fall this week is the most significant five-day drop the company has seen since going public 27 years ago.

Its market value rose by more than 470% in the past five years, peaking just a few weeks ago. It is now down by 31% against a backdrop of wider uncertainty in the tech sector.

Because of Nvidia's size and success in recent years, such a drop can have a direct impact on the savings accounts of ordinary Americans.

Nvidia's value makes up about 7% of the S&P 500 index. That index is offered as a popular index fund in US retirement savings accounts.

Those account balances rise and fall with the changes of the stock market.

Who could replace Jensen Huang as Nvidia's chief executive?

Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigns after tech giant rocked by second affair allegation

The rise and fall of Jensen Huang - how the tech superstar became mired in scandal

title: Democrats push to remove US-Israel tech measure from defense bill
excerpt: Sen. Chris Van Hollen, D-Md., is leading a push to remove provisions from the Senate and House versions of this year’s National Defense Authorization Act that would promote closer ties between the U.S...
body_text:
Sen. Chris Van Hollen, D-Md., is leading a push to remove provisions from the Senate and House versions of this year’s National Defense Authorization Act that would promote closer ties between the U.S. industrial base and Israel’s.

A letter sent Tuesday to House and Senate leadership signed by Van Hollen and 11 other Senate colleagues, including Sens. Elizabeth Warren, D-Mass., Bernie Sanders, I-Vt., and Tammy Duckworth, D-Ill., specifically addresses Section 1217 of the Senate version and Section 219 of the House version of the bill.

Those sections, called the United States-Israel Defense Cooperation Initiative in the House and the United States-Israel Framework for Upgraded Technologies, Unified Research, and Enhanced Security (FUTURES) Act in the Senate, each call for enhanced cooperation between the two countries on weapons technology development, including in artificial intelligence, quantum technology and chemical and biological weapons.

“The Senator is working with his colleagues to remove these provisions and will determine next steps should they remain in,” Van Hollen’s office said in an email to Military Times. “The Senator will continue to push to remove these provisions and push to protect the United States’ ability to act independently and in line with U.S. national security interests.”

The letter also addresses a provision of the fiscal 2027 Intelligence Authorization Act that proposes enhancing intelligence-sharing between the two countries, which, according to the text of the bill, is intended to help Israel “maintain its qualitative military edge” and “deter and counter destabilizing activities by the Government of Iran and Iran-aligned state and nonstate actors that threaten Israel, United States forces, and regional partners.”

The U.S. government’s support for Israel has come under intense scrutiny over the past three years. Israel’s war in Gaza has killed at least 74,000 Palestinians, according to Gaza’s Health Ministry, and U.S. and Israeli attacks against Iran on Feb. 28 led to a war that’s increasingly unpopular in the United States, a new Reuters/Ipsos poll found.

President Donald Trump promised to end outright military aid to Israel, which has previously come via a Memorandum of Understanding. The current MOU is set to expire in 2028 and provides billions in financing for Israel to procure U.S.-made weapons over the 10-year agreement.

Critics, including Van Hollen, have noted that the annual defense bills, as they stand, merely shift military provision from an aid model to a commercial partnership, this time overseen by the Pentagon rather than the State Department.

The new model, as proposed in the draft legislation, “would constrain the administration’s ability to independently determine how best to protect U.S. national security and would lock in long-term commitments despite our serious concerns with the Israeli government’s actions in Gaza, the West Bank, and other parts of the region,” the letter states.

The U.S. and Israel already cooperate on some defense technology; Israeli contractor Rafael Systems and Raytheon developed the David’s Sling missile interceptor system. But critics say that the proposed setup would decrease oversight of the weapons transfer system; could compromise sensitive U.S. weapons technology; and wouldn’t provide much benefit for the United States.

The NDAA is one of Congress’s “must-pass” bills, but the price tag alone — more than $1 trillion — has drawn significant pushback from Democrats. The House’s version narrowly passed in July, and Senate Democrats blocked that chamber’s version the same month, objecting to provisions for the Iran war.

In the House, Rep. Ro Khanna, D-Calif., tried unsuccessfully to pass an amendment striking the  United States-Israel Defense Cooperation Initiative when the bill was being debated in committee. Rep. Thomas Massie, R-Ky., was also a vocal opponent.

title: Pentagon ‘greenlit’ permanent presence of US troops in Poland, official says
excerpt:
The Pentagon “greenlit” the permanent presence of U.S. troops in Poland, with the final decision slated to be made by the White House in early December.

As the U.S. military reviews its force posture...
body_text:
The Pentagon “greenlit” the permanent presence of U.S. troops in Poland, with the final decision slated to be made by the White House in early December.

As the U.S. military reviews its force posture in Europe, Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth indicated to Polish officials that “everything is going in a good direction” with regard to the decision on a permanent U.S. military base in the European country, according to a recent statement released by Poland’s Ministry of National Defense following a meeting between Hegseth and Poland’s Deputy Prime Minister and Defense Minister Władysław Kosiniak-Kamysz at the Pentagon.

“The permanent presence of US troops in Poland is our absolute priority and we will not abandon this matter,” Kosiniak-Kamysz said in the release. “We will argue for this to the very end. This green light was very visible on the side of the Pentagon, in what Secretary Hegseth and his associates were saying.”

Although the final decision lies in the White House next month, Kosiniak-Kamysz said the decision is proceeding in the “best direction possible,” highlighting the teams that facilitated discussions and showcased possible locations.

President Donald Trump recently told reporters last month that the U.S. was considering the base in Poland, remarking that it was a possibility.

The Pentagon’s statement on the Tuesday talks with Polish officials did not mention a base, but it did include that the countries intend to sign an agreement that boosts military cooperations between the two countries.

It also went on to say that Kosiniak-Kamysz thanked Hegseth and the department for working to expand the presence of U.S. troops in Poland, praising the discussion on strengthening the permanent U.S. military presence in the European country.

“I would like to thank you for your commitment to the process of implementing President Donald [J.] Trump’s declaration on the deployment of [an] additional 5,000 soldiers to the territory of the Republic of Poland,” Kosiniak-Kamysz said during the meeting, the release reads.

Recently, Pentagon officials have traveled to Poland to look for potential sites to house a new base, such as Bydgoszcz, Poznań, Szczecin and Wrocław, which are all west of the Vistula River.

With a potential presence of around 5,000 service members, Poland asserts that an American base would require infrastructure that could accommodate around 25,000 people, needing construction of housing, schools and other buildings.

“We are ready,” Kosiniak-Kamysz told Polish newspaper Rzeczpospolita this week. “We have the locations prepared, we are ready to build the infrastructure, and we are ready to secure the funds.”

Polish officials have openly campaigned for a permanent American base in their country for years, dating back to when former President George W. Bush was in office from 2001 to 2009, arguing it would boost their role in NATO’s eastern flank and improve their security, which has grown especially prevalent as the war in Ukraine carries on and neighbors Poland.

In May, Pentagon officials abruptly cancelled a Poland deployment of over 4,000 soldiers, leaving Polish officials worried even as they continue to invest around $15,000 per year for the deployment of each U.S. soldier.

Poland currently hosts around 10,000 U.S. soldiers, with the majority deployed as part of a rotational presence.

Cristina Stassis is a reporter covering stories surrounding the defense industry, national security, military/veteran affairs and more. She previously worked as an editorial fellow for Defense News in 2024 where she assisted the newsroom in breaking news across Sightline Media Group.

title: Russian warship hit by Ukrainian drone in Gulf of Finland
excerpt:
The Naro-Fominsk is believed to have headed back to port in St Petersburg after the attack

Finnish officials have confirmed that a Russian warship was attacked in the Gulf of Finland on Wednesday, al...
body_text:
The Naro-Fominsk is believed to have headed back to port in St Petersburg after the attack

Finnish officials have confirmed that a Russian warship was attacked in the Gulf of Finland on Wednesday, although little is known about the strike.

Ukraine's SBU security service said it targeted the ship Naro-Fominsk as part of a broader drone operation against Russia's Ust-Luga oil export depot on the Baltic coast.

The attack, thought to be the first time Ukrainian drones have attacked a Russian ship in an area of the Baltic Sea open to civilian maritime traffic, has raised questions about whether Ukraine could expand its strikes.

Helsinki has been one of Kyiv's closest European allies, and Finnish officials have described the incident as a direct result of Russia's continued full-scale war.

Finland's military has given few details of the incident, but it appears to have taken place in a narrow stretch some distance from the Finnish coast.

The country's Foreign Minister Elina Valtonen was adamant that the situation in the Baltic Sea remained stable and safe and that there was no threat of any kind to marine traffic.

Defence officials are understood to have stressed to Kyiv that the Gulf is a relatively narrow waterway used by oil tankers and civilian vessels, and is also home to subsea data cables.

Ukraine's SBU described the Russian ship as a Buyan-M type small corvette that carried Kalibr and Oniks cruise missiles. There were also unconfirmed reports of Russian combat helicopters being destroyed.

Martin Herem, the defence minister of Estonia, which borders the Gulf, told public broadcaster ERR that the ship was hit at about 05:30 (03:30 GMT) on Wednesday but did not say how it was attacked: "We know that smoke came from the ship afterwards. The ship itself went back towards St Petersburg."

The extent of casualties or damage sustained by the Russian navy ship remains unclear, and Moscow rarely gives such details.

"The Baltic Sea fleet has been untouched up to this point but there seemingly was a window of opportunity for Ukraine and they understandably tried to use it," said military analyst Emil Kastehelmi, co-founder of the Black Bird monitoring group.

Russian and Ukrainian vessels have been repeatedly targeted in the Black Sea since Russia's full-scale invasion began in February 2022, but even though the latest strike on a ship in the Baltic is unprecedented, Kastehelmi told the BBC he did not consider it a serious escalation.

Ukrainian drones are regularly launched into Russia from northern Ukraine. Several storage tanks at the Ust-Luga terminal are thought to have been hit overnight on Wednesday and fires at the port were visible over the border in Estonia.

Herem said Ukrainian drones attacked the Ust-Luga region from midnight until about 06:00, mostly flying close to the Estonian border but still in Russian airspace.

He added that one drone had entered Estonian airspace briefly from Latvia and then headed towards Russia.

Nato aircraft based in the Baltic states were in the air at the time, but Herem said it had not been considered safe for them to destroy the drones.

Ukrainian foreign ministry spokesman Heorhiy Tykhyy said late on Wednesday that Moscow's allegations that Kyiv had used the airspace of the Baltic states to attack Russia were "baseless", although he acknowledged "incidents might occur when Russia diverts drones from its airspace using electronic warfare".

title: Soldier who scolded Hegseth's entourage at Tomb of Unknown Soldier receives special honor from Pentagon chief
excerpt: A soldier guarding the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier reminded visitors to maintain silence and respect after laughter was heard during a photo session involving Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth's entourag...
body_text:
A soldier guarding the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier reminded visitors to maintain silence and respect after laughter was heard during a photo session involving Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth's entourage.

Secretary of War Pete Hegseth on Thursday awarded a medal to the Army soldier who reprimanded him and his entourage at the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier after laughter was heard from the group on Veterans Day.

"We love soldiers. We love standards," Hegseth wrote Thursday in a post on X. "Well done, Specialist."

A Pentagon official confirmed to Fox News Digital in a Thursday statement that Hegseth had "proudly" awarded Spc. Thomas Iglesias the medal for "the execution of his duties."

Secretary of War Pete Hegseth awards a medal to the soldier who reprimanded him at Arlington National Cemetery on Wednesday. (@SecWar/X)

TRUMP DEFENDS PENTAGON CHIEF AS MASSIE TARGETS HIM: 'HEGSETH SHOULD BE PRAISED, NOT IMPEACHED'

"As shown in the photos, Secretary Hegseth welcomed the 3rd U.S. Infantry Regiment, the Old Guard, to the Pentagon where he proudly awarded Specialist Thomas Iglesias the Joint Service Commendation Medal for the execution of his duties at the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier on November 11, 2026," the official said.

The Joint Service Commendation Medal is awarded to members of the military who distinguish themselves through meritorious achievement or service, typically while serving in joint military operations or activities.

The award comes after video from Wednesday showed Iglesias reminding visitors to remain silent and maintain decorum after laughter was heard as Hegseth and his entourage walked away from the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier following a Veterans Day ceremony.

"All visitors will maintain an atmosphere of silence and respect at all times," the soldier commanded to the entourage at the time.

Secretary of War Pete Hegseth awards a medal to Spc. Thomas Iglesias at the Pentagon. (@SecWar/X)

TUNNEL TO TOWERS PAYS OFF MORTGAGES FOR 30 MILITARY FAMILIES IN VETERANS DAY TRIBUTE: 'A GREAT SACRIFICE'

Following the incident on Wednesday, Pentagon spokesman Sean Parnell told CBS News that Hegseth and "the entire Department have always honored-and will always honor-the sacrifices our military men and women have made to keep America safe."

Secretary of War Pete Hegseth meets with soldiers at the Pentagon on Thursday. (@SecWar/X)

"While commemorating this solemn day, a soldier correctly and respectfully reminded everyone to maintain decorum," Parnell added.

title: Russian court jails rights lawyer for 12 years on treason charge
excerpt: A court in Russia’s Baltic exclave of Kaliningrad has sentenced a 66-year-old rights lawyer to 12 years in prison for treason, after prosecutors accused her of passing sensitive information to Ukraine...
body_text:
A court in Russia’s Baltic exclave of Kaliningrad has sentenced a 66-year-old rights lawyer to 12 years in prison for treason, after prosecutors accused her of passing sensitive information to Ukraine.

The court imposed the sentence on Thursday on Maria Bontsler, according to the rights group Slovo Zashchite, which said she had worked with a number of defendants accused of political offences in Kaliningrad.

The territory sits on the Baltic Sea between Lithuania and Poland.

A court statement posted on Telegram did not name her, but said she had been detained by the FSB intelligence agency on allegations of passing information to Ukraine beginning in 2024 about security officers in Kaliningrad.

Prosecutors also alleged she gave Ukraine information on criminal cases in the exclave that were of interest to Kyiv, the statement said.

She was also given an extra year of restrictions on her activity. Prosecutors had sought 15 years, according to Slovo Zashchite.

Slovo Zashchite said the trial was held behind closed doors, with Bontsler and her lawyers prevented from attending, and that she was allowed only to make a closing statement. It said her lawyers argued that none of the information cited by prosecutors was secret, and that she had been in ill health in detention.

Since Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022, parliament has approved laws that make public actions aimed at “discrediting” the army illegal and ban the spread of “fake news” about the armed forces.

Russian courts have also jailed lawyers who took on politically sensitive cases. In January 2025, a court sentenced three lawyers of the late opposition leader Alexey Navalny to between three and a half and five and a half years on “extremism” charges, in a case widely seen as an effort to discourage defence lawyers from taking political cases.

title: Locked On Vikings podcaster gets destroyed on social media for anti-Kirk Cousins take
excerpt: The Minnesota Vikings traded for Kirk Cousins and will face the Green Bay Packers on Sunday. Nick Wright, Chris Broussard, and Kevin Wildes ask if the favored Packers are on upset alert, and they disc...
body_text:
The Minnesota Vikings traded for Kirk Cousins and will face the Green Bay Packers on Sunday. Nick Wright, Chris Broussard, and Kevin Wildes ask if the favored Packers are on upset alert, and they discuss Micah Parsons saying that Drake Maye has "gone from potential MVP to the struggle bus".

With the recent trade that sent quarterback Kirk Cousins back to Minnesota, there are a lot of people in the Land of 10,000 Lakes feeling pretty nostalgic these last few days.

After all, Cousins was selected to three Pro Bowls with the Vikings and won them their most recent playoff game.

This page may contain affiliate links to legal sports betting partners. If you sign up or place a wager, FOX News may be compensated. This content was created by a team that works independently from the FOX newsroom.

But not everyone wearing purple and gold is on board with the optimism surrounding Mr. Cousins, and one of those Debbie Downers happens to be Locked on Vikings podcast host Luke Braun.

KIRK COUSINS REVEALS TOUCHING DECISION HIS SONS MADE AFTER TRADE TO VIKINGS: 'LET'S GO!'

Kirk Cousins celebrates on the field after the Minnesota Vikings defeated the Indianapolis Colts at U.S. Bank Stadium in Minneapolis, Minnesota, on Dec. 17, 2022. (Getty Images)

Braun took to social media on Tuesday lamenting the move from his beloved Vikings, calling the trade his "long personal nightmare."

"I was always a big Kirk hater when he was here in Minnesota," Braun admits. "Because I thought, hey, this guy is not going to lead us to the promised land."

NFL TRADE DEADLINE WINNERS AND LOSERS, INCLUDING DIANNA RUSSINI AND KIRK COUSINS

The podcaster brought up Cousins' supposed turnover problems and the fact that the Vikings need to protect the ball and stop putting their defense in bad situations.

There's a lot wrong with what Braun said, particularly with the fact that Cousins is statistically one of the safer quarterbacks when it comes to committing turnovers, and the internet saw right through his reasoning.

VIKINGS' CARSON WENTZ WAS HISTORICALLY AWFUL IN LOSS TO BILLS, POSTING A STAT LINE DIFFICULT TO COMPREHEND

Las Vegas Raiders quarterback Kirk Cousins warms up before an NFL preseason game against the San Francisco 49ers on Thursday, Aug. 27, 2026, in Las Vegas. (AP Photo/David Becker)

Normally, this is the part of the article where I break down everything Braun said that was incorrect, but the fine folks on X stole my thunder and did it for me.

Let's start with Braun's "turnover" claim, which many commenters pointed out is just not true.

Hmmm, okay. So either Braun is misinformed, or there's something deeper to this Kirk Cousins hate that he isn't mentioning.

Of course, the commenters came with receipts for that as well, pointing out that Braun has been a vocal liberal (something that clashes with Cousins' overt Christian family values) and even cited screenshots from his BlueSky account trashing the Wilfs family for the trade and mentioning Michelle Tafoya's political campaign.

If your reaction to the Vikings going from Kyler Murray to Kirk Cousins is one of disgust, there are probably some deeper, non-football related reasons for it.

MINNESOTA VIKINGS' SOFT BENCHING OF KYLER MURRAY LEADS TO CARSON WENTZ TAKING OVER AS NEW STARTING QB

Minnesota Vikings quarterback Kirk Cousins looks on from the bench during the second quarter against the Detroit Lions at U.S. Bank Stadium in Minneapolis, Minn., on Dec. 24, 2023. (USA TODAY Sports via Reuters Con)

Is Kirk Cousins Joe Montana? No, nor is anyone claiming he is.

But if Cousins can keep up his numbers from the first nine games of the season coupled with Minnesota's defense, the Vikings have a chance to make some noise this postseason.

title: Pat Cummins press conference live updates: Australian cricket captain speaks about Usman Khawaja’s ‘sandpapergate’ claims
excerpt:
Cummins speaks about allegations in Usman Khawaja’s book about the 2018 ball-tampering incident

Cummins says he was “genuinely shocked” this week amid the comments in Khawaja’s book. He went on:

dou...
body_text:
Cummins speaks about allegations in Usman Khawaja’s book about the 2018 ball-tampering incident

Cummins says he was “genuinely shocked” this week amid the comments in Khawaja’s book. He went on:

double quotation markWhen he says we all knew, if [by] that he means we knew sandpaper was going out on the field, he’s 100% wrong. I said that consistently for the last eight years. I did not know that was happening …

He says that I and others were architects of a scheme to ball-tamper with sandpaper. That’s complete and utter nonsense.

Cummins goes on to say he believes Khawaja’s book has “been casual with my [life] and the lives of many others, and I think Australian cricket”.

Cummins said the past series at the centre of the initial controversy took place during a “lawless” era.

“I’m glad we have not seen a series like that since,” he said.

This press conference is approaching 45 minutes. Cummins says he’ll stay until journalists had exhausted all of their questions, and then hopefully move on permanently from the rehashed controversy.

Cummins says it seems the issue has been ‘sitting heavy’ on Khawaja

Cummins won’t say much about any exchanges he’s had with Khawaja this week, saying they’re personal conversations and he doesn’t want to “go into it”.

When asked why he thinks the revelations are coming out now, Cummins says:

double quotation markIt looks like it’s been sitting heavy on him for a while. It’s eight and a half years ago. I get that … Maybe this is Usman’s chance and he never really got over it at the time.

But he reiterates that he believes the claims are “irresponsible”.

Cummins said he’s been frustrated Khawaja’s book is relitigating an episode from more than eight years ago, adding it had reopened trauma for some:

double quotation markIt’s eight and a half years, we have moved on.

We’ll keep saying it but, again, these are people’s lives. It was traumatic for some of them. They have had to work through quite a bit to get out the other side.

So again, that’s why I’m really disappointed and frustrated this week … how it’s been dealt with so flippantly.

Cummins says there’s a ‘proper way to do things’

Cummins says he believes there was a proper way to handle the sandpaper incident, pointing to the Cricket Australia investigation shortly afterwards.

Cricket Australia’s chief executive, Todd Greenberg, told media this week there was not “any compelling reason” to revisit the investigation, even though there are “specific details” in Khawaja’s book “that contradict the versions that have been provided by others”.

double quotation markThere’s a very proper way to do things and improve. I think that investigation was a proper way to do it.

Everyone was asked in the circumstances about a game very quickly after. So that’s for CA. I think you can maybe argue whether the judgements were fair, but what can you do? I got asked all the questions, answered them all fairly.

A reporter just asked about the difference in stories. Cummins replied:

double quotation markThat’s my story, so I think he’s wrong.

He went on to say there appeared to be a “few big leaps” in the book and Khawaja had been “vague” and acted in a “very casual matter”:

double quotation markThe details really matter in that difference. So perhaps there was conversations with Cameron Bancroft around taking sandpaper out and how to do it. That doesn’t mean that everyone in that dressing room knew what was going on.

double quotation markThere was no master plan around using illegal methods. I think that’s maybe something that hasn’t been spoken about enough. People assume you have gone from very legal methods to suddenly taking sandpaper and then there must have been some huge master plan.

There’s no grand plan, there’s no team meeting, there’s no bowlers saying ‘this is what must happen’.

Cummins: ‘I did not see anything on the ball’

Cummins was asked how the ball looked at the time.

double quotation markAt that stage, you know, even the umpires had a look. We didn’t know it had been altered with sandpaper.

Balls get roughened up every time we play. So, you know, whether that’s from a foreign object or something that’s totally legal and part of the game. Sometimes it’s hard to know. But out there in the field I did not see anything on the ball.

Cummins says he was “genuinely shocked” this week amid the comments in Khawaja’s book. He went on:

double quotation markWhen he says we all knew, if [by] that he means we knew sandpaper was going out on the field, he’s 100% wrong. I said that consistently for the last eight years. I did not know that was happening …

He says that I and others were architects of a scheme to ball-tamper with sandpaper. That’s complete and utter nonsense.

Cummins goes on to say he believes Khawaja’s book has “been casual with my [life] and the lives of many others, and I think Australian cricket”.

Khawaja memoir ‘readable, surprisingly revealing, sometimes painfully frank’

Gideon Haigh, writing for the Guardian this week, says the greatest shame of the controversy inflamed by Usman Khawaja’s memoir, Sabr, is that “99% of those opining about it will never read it”.

double quotation markThey will experience it by quotes and summaries, magnified and distorted, elided and exaggerated, shaped by voyeurism and schadenfreude.

In fact, Sabr is a readable, surprisingly revealing, sometimes painfully frank book about a unique career.

Haigh says Khawaja was among the most talented batters in an Australian generation “when it was not in oversupply”, but points out he played in only 22% of the national team’s total fixtures over that period.

double quotation markIf he developed a carapace to deal with such endless disappointment, should that surprise anyone?

Sabr might mean patience or resilience in Urdu, but a strength of Khawaja’s testament is that he allows the impatience to show through.

It is a cranky book because, perhaps, a degree of crankiness is what it takes to come back and back and back, when one is never sure one’s abilities are appreciated and one’s face fits.

Starc statement: ‘we weren’t aware of things being taken on the field’

Earlier this week, Mitchell Starc denied claims made in Khawaja’s book.

Starc broke his silence to address Khawaja’s comments, saying he was not aware that sandpaper was used in the Test before Cape Town, nor during the Newlands match. The paceman said his recollection of the match had not changed from what the bowlers said in a statement issued in 2021, which denied all knowledge of the ball-tampering plan.

double quotation markAs far as our statement said, we weren’t aware of things being taken on the field, that’s where I’ll leave it. We weren’t aware anything was taken on to the field to be tampered with. We saw [the sandpaper] on the big screen in Cape Town.

As far as the book is concerned, I haven’t read it. I probably won’t read it. So that’s for Usman to elaborate on.

I’ll stick to what I said five years ago, what I said at the time, eight years ago. Clearly, there’s different versions from different people, and I’ll leave it where I left it back then.

In 2018, during the third Test against South Africa in Cape Town, Australia’s opening batter, Cameron Bancroft, was caught on TV using sandpaper against one side of the cricket ball.

An investigation revealed the tampering was planned by the captain, Steve Smith, and vice-captain, David Warner. Both, as well as Bancroft, received bans from international and local cricket.

Fast-forward to now – and former Australian batter Usman Khawaja alleged in his autobiography, Sabr: Finding My Way in Cricket and Life, that the use of sandpaper was widespread.

Khawaja alleged the tampering happened earlier in the series at Port Elizabeth and that the entire team knew about it. Cummins has not commented – until now.

The Australian cricket captain, Pat Cummins, is to speak for the first time on the sandpaper scandal since allegations about ball tampering from his former teammate Usman Khawaja.

Cummins posted to social media that he would speak to reporters on Friday morning at Cricket NSW’s headquarters in Sydney.

double quotation markI’m training at Cricket Central tomorrow morning before the Blues play in the Shield match.

Happy to speak with any and all media about the events of this week at 9.30 am.

I’ve taken some time to try and better understand the long list and full extent of Uzzy’s allegations so I can respond properly.

Afterwards please stay and support the Blues!

title: Former owner of Peanut the squirrel, viral pet euthanized by NY officials, detained by ICE
excerpt:
Fox News host Greg Gutfeld and the panel discuss the news surrounding internet sensation ‘Peanut the Squirrel,’ who was confiscated and killed by New York state officials on ‘Gutfeld!’

The wife of th...
body_text:
Fox News host Greg Gutfeld and the panel discuss the news surrounding internet sensation ‘Peanut the Squirrel,’ who was confiscated and killed by New York state officials on ‘Gutfeld!’

The wife of the New York man whose viral pet squirrel Peanut was seized and euthanized by wildlife officials in 2024 has been detained by immigration authorities.

Daniela Bittner, a German native, was arrested by U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) in mid-October at a small airport near New York's border with Pennsylvania, according to The Associated Press (AP).

She and her husband of four years, Mark Longo, were planning to attend a TikTok event when officers approached them, according to the New York Post.

Longo said his wife's detention stemmed from what he described as a minor paperwork issue, The AP said. The couple reportedly made an error on one of her immigration forms and failed to catch it while dealing with the seizure and euthanasia of Peanut.

OWNERS OF BELOVED PEANUT THE SQUIRREL PLAN TO SUE NEW YORK STATE OVER SEIZURE AND KILLING BY AUTHORITIES

Mark Longo, center, and his wife Daniela Bittner, left, speak during a news conference on April 8, 2025, in Albany, N.Y. Bittner’s husband says her ICE detention stems from a paperwork error. (AP Photo/Michael Hill)

"She came into this country legally on a visa. We filed the paperwork and stuff and apparently the government is saying we filed the wrong piece of paper," Longo told The Post.

"They had asked for additional information, which we provided, and then apparently they sent a letter stating that it was denied because we filed the wrong paperwork, which we never received," he said.

"This is a minor paperwork issue and it’s being treated as if my wife literally crawled out a hole to get into this country," he added.

PEANUT THE PET SQUIRREL TAKEN AWAY BY NEW YORK STATE OFFICIALS FROM ADOPTED HOME, MAY BE EUTHANIZED

Peanut was rescued at 5 weeks old by his adoptive human parents after his mother was run over by a car. (peanut_the_squirrel12 via Instagram)

Longo said Bittner has no criminal history and was hit with the maximum penalty, potentially facing deportation without a hearing, according to The Post.

The couple reportedly married in 2022, shortly after Bittner returned to Germany to resolve a visa situation.

The Department of Homeland Security (DHS) told the outlet that Bittner lawfully entered the U.S. multiple times between May 2021 and November 2022, each time receiving permission to stay for a temporary period.

However, DHS said she was arrested because she "chose to overstay her welcome in defiance of our nation's laws."

"To be clear, a pending application does not confer legal status in the United States," DHS told the Post.

Bittner has reportedly been transferred between several detention centers, from Syracuse to Buffalo, Louisiana and eventually Texas.

Longo described the conditions his wife has faced in federal custody as "deplorable," The AP said.

Her arrest has also cast uncertainty over the couple's nonprofit animal rescue operation, where Bittner reportedly cares for 600 animals rescued from neglect.

"If my wife gets deported for a paperwork issue, we will lose EVERYTHING we worked for. Our Nonprofit Animal Sanctuary will close and 600 animals will have to find another home. All we wanted was to be left alone. We finally moved on from the tragic murder of Pnut, now to this," he said.

Peanut the squirrel enjoys some peanuts in this photo shared on Instagram. (peanut_the_squirrel12 via Instagram)

The couple found themselves at the center of a nationwide wildlife controversy in 2024 after New York wildlife officials seized and euthanized their pet squirrel, sparking widespread outrage.

Longo had rescued Peanut when he was just 5 weeks old after the squirrel's mother was reportedly struck and killed by a car. The animal later became a viral social media sensation, amassing a large following online.

The Associated Press contributed to this report.

Bonny Chu is a Breaking and Trending News Writer for Fox News Digital

title: Democrat Cindy Holscher wins Kansas governor's race, extending party's hold on governor's mansion
excerpt:
Democratic state Sen. Cindy Holscher will become Kansas’ next governor after defeating Republican Ty Masterson in the Nov. 3 election, The Associated Press projected Thursday. (REUTERS)

Democratic st...
body_text:
Democratic state Sen. Cindy Holscher will become Kansas’ next governor after defeating Republican Ty Masterson in the Nov. 3 election, The Associated Press projected Thursday. (REUTERS)

Democratic state Sen. Cindy Holscher won the Kansas governor’s race, defeating Republican Kansas Senate President Ty Masterson in the open contest to succeed term-limited Democratic Gov. Laura Kelly, The Associated Press projected.The victory keeps the governor’s mansion in Democratic hands and marks the third consecutive Kansas gubernatorial election won by a Democrat. Kelly won the office in 2018 and secured a second term in 2022.Holscher has served in the Kansas Senate since 2021 after previously spending four years in the state House. She secured the Democratic nomination after defeating fellow state Sen. Ethan Corson, who was endorsed by Kelly and former Democratic Gov. Kathleen Sebelius, in the August primary.Holscher faced scrutiny during the campaign over resurfaced social media posts from 2023 in which she suggested Jesus Christ could have been transgender. The comments came during a debate over proposed Kansas legislation restricting drag performances in front of children.

CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APPHolscher defeated Masterson, who was endorsed by President Donald Trump in the crowded GOP primary and has served as president of the state Senate since 2021.

Brittany Miller is a Fox News Digital breaking news writer and former Independent reporter who graduated from Syracuse University in 2023.

title: Chargers coach Jim Harbaugh tees off on Broncos for backing out of trade post deadline: 'Bad precedent'
excerpt: The Los Angeles Chargers are 0-7, and Nick Wright has called them the "biggest disappointment in NFL history." Chris Broussard and Kevin Wildes discuss this take and ask if it’s valid, and they discus...
body_text:
The Los Angeles Chargers are 0-7, and Nick Wright has called them the "biggest disappointment in NFL history." Chris Broussard and Kevin Wildes discuss this take and ask if it’s valid, and they discuss Shedeur Sanders being in line to start for the Cleveland Browns as Deshaun Watson is in concussion protocol.

Los Angeles Chargers head coach Jim Harbaugh called out the Denver Broncos after a trade involving linebacker Daiyan Henley fell through.

The Chargers agreed to trade Henley for a 2027 fourth-round pick and a 2028 fifth-round pick, but Harbaugh said the Broncos wanted to change the 2028 pick compensation based on a pass-fail medical grade.

This page may contain affiliate links to legal sports betting partners. If you sign up or place a wager, FOX News may be compensated. This content was created by a team that works independently from the FOX newsroom.

"The Broncos based a pass-fail on a medical grade, based on whether we would take less compensation, and we wouldn’t, and we didn’t," Harbaugh told reporters Thursday. "In my opinion, it’s one of those loopholes that the league should really look into because it sets a bad precedent, continues to set a bad precedent."

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

Los Angeles Chargers linebacker Daiyan Henley returns an interception against the Houston Texans during the second quarter at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood, Calif., on Nov. 8, 2026. (IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect)

The Broncos were given approval to revisit the terms of the deal with the Chargers after consulting with the NFL on Wednesday, according to The Athletic. The Broncos' medical evaluation of Henley after the trade did not match the Chargers' evaluation before the teams agreed to terms, according to the report.

Harbaugh criticized the Broncos, saying they would have passed Henley on his medical evaluation in exchange for less compensation. He also said the NFL needs to close the loophole.

"Really, it shouldn’t be (a loophole), but apparently it is," Harbaugh said. "That’s why it’s a loophole and teams should not have the ability to do that. I mean, it’s a medical grade. It’s a pass-fail for a medical grade. They told us they weren’t going to pass him if it was a fourth and a fifth, which was agreed upon, and they would not pass him for that. They would pass him for a fourth and a … fill in the blank. I don’t know what to call that."

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

Los Angeles Chargers head coach Jim Harbaugh reacts from the sideline during the second half of an NFL football game against the Arizona Cardinals on Sunday, Sept. 13, 2026, in Inglewood, Calif. (AP Photo/Caroline Brehman)

The 26-year-old linebacker was on the injury report in Week 9 with a shoulder injury but played 61 of the team's 70 defensive snaps. Harbaugh said he was thrilled to have Henley back.

"He was welcomed back with open arms, and happy about that," Harbaugh said. "What that put Daiyan through, you know, kind of the ringer for the last couple days. Yeah, it’s emotional. It’s painful. And all that’s considered and should be considered by the league when they look into this loophole."

OUTKICK IS NOW AVAILABLE ON THE FOX NEWS APP: CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD

Los Angeles Chargers linebacker Daiyan Henley returns an interception against the Houston Texans during the second quarter at SoFi Stadium. (Gary A. Vasquez, IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect)

Harbaugh said Henley was back in meetings Thursday. Henley is in his fourth season with the Chargers after being selected in the third round of the 2023 NFL Draft out of Washington State.

In 56 career games, Henley has 317 combined tackles, five sacks, four interceptions and one forced fumble.

title: Donald Trump Jr exits as paid adviser for prediction market Kalshi
excerpt:
Kalshi announces ‘mutual decision’ as Democrats say they plan to investigate Trump family’s investments

Donald Trump Jr is no longer a paid adviser for Kalshi, the prediction market company said Thur...
body_text:
Kalshi announces ‘mutual decision’ as Democrats say they plan to investigate Trump family’s investments

Donald Trump Jr is no longer a paid adviser for Kalshi, the prediction market company said Thursday.

Kalshi described it as a mutual business decision between the two parties that followed a decision by Trump Jr’s investment firm, 1789 Capital, to increase its investment in Kalshi’s biggest competitor Polymarket.

But the announcement comes a week after Democrats were able to take control of both the House and Senate in the midterm elections.

Democrats have said they planned to investigate the Trump family’s investments, including their business relationships with both prediction markets.

“We have mutually agreed to end Don’s advisory role after his firm’s significant investment in a competitor this past summer,” said Dani Lever, a spokesperson for Kalshi. “We are grateful for his contributions in helping us market Kalshi to more customers.”

The president’s eldest son became a paid “strategic adviser” for Kalshi shortly after President Trump was sworn into office for his second term in January 2025 and has been an investor in Polymarket since August 2025. Both companies have seen their popularity and use jump significantly in the past two years.

At the same time, both companies have received favorable treatment from the White House. The Commodity Futures Trading Commission has backed the industry’s efforts to expand their products nationwide, including allowing their customers to trade sports-related contracts.

Both companies have adamantly denied that the financial relationship between Polymarket, Kalshi and the Trumps played any role in how the industry has been regulated under this administration.

1789 Capital increased its investment in Polymarket this past August, as part of Polymarket’s latest fundraising round. It was this investment that started the conversation about ending Trump Jr’s advisory role with Kalshi.

title: Jared Verse believes a mental block is affecting his play, seeks psychiatrist's help to address it
excerpt:
The Cleveland Browns have traded Myles Garrett to the Los Angeles Rams for Jared Verse and a 2027 1st-round pick. Colin Cowherd reacts to the trade and asks if this was a good deal.

Jared Verse has z...
body_text:
The Cleveland Browns have traded Myles Garrett to the Los Angeles Rams for Jared Verse and a 2027 1st-round pick. Colin Cowherd reacts to the trade and asks if this was a good deal.

Jared Verse has zero sacks, zero forced fumbles and zero fumble recoveries for the Cleveland Browns this season, and the defensive end believes a mental block could be contributing to his struggles.

Verse, 26, told reporters on Thursday he is working on himself to overcome the frustration he’s feeling over his lack of production. And that work isn’t about lifting more weights, improving his technique or studying his opponents more closely.

"I think it was definitely a mental block," Verse said. "I train my body every day to push myself to the limits of what I’m physically capable of doing. So I don’t think it was any issue with my body, but I think I’ve taken the steps to figure out what it was."

CLEVELAND BROWNS RESET UNDER TODD MONKEN AFTER TRADING MYLES GARRETT AND PARTING WITH STEFANSKI

Maxx Crosby and Jared Verse look on during annual Sack Summit event in Las Vegas. (Raising Cane's)

The steps Verse has taken, he said, include meeting with Browns team psychiatrist Mayur Pandya to address his mental health.

"Obviously, like, I'm upset with the way I've been playing," Verse said. "I don't think it's anything physical. There's nothing wrong with my body. It's not like that. I think it was a mental aspect of the game."

Verse declined to explain exactly how he’s addressing the problem with Pandya but believes he’s close to turning a corner as a result.

New Orleans Saints offensive tackle Kelvin Banks Jr. (71) engages with Cleveland Browns defensive end Jared Verse (8) during an NFL game on Sunday, Nov. 8, 2026, at the Caesars Superdome in New Orleans, La. (Peter Forest/Sipa USA via Reuters Connect)

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

"I think I've attacked it very well these last couple weeks, but I think this past week is a big key thing that I've done is I'm very excited for this next week," Verse said.

"I took a lot of time for self-growth. I met with Dr. Pandya a little bit, and I figured out what my issue was."

Times have truly changed in American society.

The Greatest Generation went to war, defeated the Nazis of Germany and the imperialists of Japan and stamped the United States as the strongest country on the planet, all at a great cost to their mental and physical health, but seemingly never complained about it.

But athletes today struggle with contracts, or statistics, or their home lives, and do not hesitate to have their mental health checked.

But it could also be seen in some sectors — particularly in the high-octane NFL — as weakness.

Los Angeles Rams linebacker Jared Verse (8) strips the ball from Indianapolis Colts quarterback Daniel Jones (17) during the second hall of an NFL football game Sunday, Sept. 28, 2025, in Inglewood, California. (AP Photo/Marcio Jose Sanchez)

Verse seemed to touch on that by suggesting there are limits to what is acceptable as individuals address their mental health.

"You can't go out there and start doing some crazy things like going to, like, I'm training with a monk or something that," he said.

But, clearly, professional mental help is something Verse believes is about to help him change the narrative of his 2026 season.

"I think the Browns fans are upset about it, I'm upset about it, I think we all have a reason to be upset," he said. "I just haven't done enough, and I think I'll take any time to figure out what the issue was. I've attacked it. I think I'm ready for this week."

Armando Salguero is OutKick's Senior NFL Writer.

title: Human vs. ChatGPT NFL Week 10 betting picks: Ice-cold human seeks a rebound as AI gains ground
excerpt:
Tom Brady lists his top 10 teams for Week 9 which include the Chicago Bears, San Francisco 49ers, Kansas City Chiefs and more!

I am officially ice cold. I followed up the disaster that was Week 8 (wh...
body_text:
Tom Brady lists his top 10 teams for Week 9 which include the Chicago Bears, San Francisco 49ers, Kansas City Chiefs and more!

I am officially ice cold. I followed up the disaster that was Week 8 (which I’m still not talking about) with a losing slate in Week 9. This serves as an important reminder to everyone out there: being a winning bettor in the NFL is very, very difficult.

It’s hard to find value because the NFL is one of the most heavily bet leagues in the country. There’s an enormous amount of information available, and both sportsbooks and sharp bettors spend all week picking these games apart.

This page may contain affiliate links to legal sports betting partners. If you sign up or place a wager, FOX News may be compensated. This content was created by a team that works independently from the FOX newsroom.

NFL WEEK 9 SUNDAY TAKEAWAYS: BENGALS, 49ERS, PACKERS LOOK SUPER; RAMS FINALLY OVER .500

The books are very good at pricing NFL bets, so the edges are difficult to find. I think there’s more room to find value in less-bet markets, like college basketball games featuring unranked and lesser-known schools.

Does that mean we’re going to quit? Of course not. A profitable season in NFL betting, especially when I’ve committed to five bets per week, is something worth bragging about. So the goal is to get back to profitability.

It feels like I've been losing more than Eagles head coach Nick Sirianni over the past two weeks. (Icon Sportswire via Getty Images)

Both of us get five selections from the same odds board, with no bet priced worse than -120. Odds were taken from the board supplied Thursday at noon ET.

Stakes are adjusted so every winning bet produces one unit of profit. For example, -110 requires risking 1.10 units, while +110 requires approximately 0.91 units. A push returns the stake and counts as zero units.

The Denver Broncos once again benefited from some questionable officiating, and it helped sink our Panthers bet. I’m not bitter, though. The Raiders and Vikings were clean whiffs, and the latter served as a very important reminder: never wager your hard-earned money on Carson Wentz.

If you remove GPT’s worst two weeks (Week 1 and Week 8), the robot is having an OK year: 18-16-1 and up 0.77 units. Unfortunately for the AI, we don’t just forget about the disasters. Unfortunately for me, too, because I’d love to dump that Week 8 stinker (which I’m still not talking about).

Dan Z.’s Plug Your Nose and Hit ‘Place Bet’ Bet of the Week: 5-3, +1.83 units

At least the Bucs got the Plug Your Nose bet back in the win column. Small victories.

Washington Commanders at New York Giants, Thursday Night Football

Betting a road team on Thursday Night Football is always scary, but I’m a Jayden Daniels truther. What can I say? J.J. McCarthy has given the New York Giants some life, and John Harbaugh remains one of the NFL’s best coaches. But New York has also been incredibly fortunate to reach 5-2-1, with four of those wins coming against the Cowboys, Titans, Cardinals and Eagles.

I'm a Jayden Daniels truther. (Getty Images)

Washington hung tough against the Rams last week and held a second-half lead. I think Daniels wills the Commanders to a win Thursday night, but I’ll still take the two points just in case they tie again. That’s a joke. Kind of.

Jayden Daniels hurt the Giants with his legs in the first meeting, and that’s Washington’s best answer to New York’s blitz. I worry about how much the Commanders can get on the ground from anyone else with Jacory Croskey-Merritt out. I passed because even a three-point Giants win is enough to beat this ticket.

New England Patriots vs. Detroit Lions, Sunday at 9:30 a.m. ET, in Munich

New England headed to Munich a day ahead of Detroit, and I think that works in the Patriots’ favor. Plus, they’re coming off a terrible performance against the Green Bay Packers, and I think they’ll be extremely motivated to prove that was a fluke.

The Lions have won four straight, but I’m still not sold on Detroit. For an offense that’s supposed to be among the most explosive in the league, the Lions are actually winning with defense and haven’t scored more than 20 points in their past three games. I don’t think that’s going to work against Mike Vrabel’s squad, so I’ll take the points with the Pats.

I lean New England here. Drake Maye can attack a Detroit secondary that’s given up plenty of big plays, and getting the full field goal matters in a game I expect to be close. Detroit’s pass rush against New England’s protection is what kept me off it at -115.

Houston Texans at Cleveland Browns, Sunday at 1 p.m. ET

The Browns just aren’t that good. I said it. Having a quarterback controversy between Deshaun Watson and Shedeur Sanders perfectly encapsulates where this team finds itself through nine weeks. Watson has been named the starter against Houston, but that doesn’t make me feel any better about Cleveland.

SHEDEUR SANDERS MAKES CASE TO REPLACE DESHAUN WATSON IN BROWNS' OVERTIME LOSS TO SAINTS

The Texans haven't been super impressive, either, but this team is much better than Cleveland. Even on the road, I think the Texans win by at least a touchdown.

Houston’s pass rush is the best reason to lay the points. The Texans have 29 sacks, and Cleveland has struggled to protect its quarterbacks. Deshaun Watson’s return gives the Browns a better chance to hang around, and their defense can keep the game close. I lean Houston, but I’d want -4½.

Miami Dolphins at Indianapolis Colts, Sunday at 1 p.m. ET

I know what you’re thinking: "Are you nuts?!" This is a game featuring Kyle McCord and Daniel Jones as the starting quarterbacks, and the Colts have traded Quenton Nelson, Josh Downs and Keenan Allen.

But I have a sneaking suspicion that Jonathan Taylor is due for a vintage JT game and will help the Colts put some points on the board. Plus, McCord and Jones are each liable to make a mistake or two that leads to easy scoring opportunities for the other team.

Jonathan Taylor is due for a huge game with multiple explosive plays, which is why I like the over in this one. (Getty Images)

For the first time, Dan Z.’s Plug Your Nose and Hit ‘Place Bet’ Bet of the Week is a total. Because, again, we’re counting on teams quarterbacked by Kyle McCord and Daniel Jones to combine for at least 39 points.

This nearly made my card. Jonathan Taylor has a good matchup against a Miami front that lost Zach Sieler, and 20-19 gets you over. My hesitation is how much Miami can contribute in Kyle McCord’s first NFL start. Indianapolis also just traded Keenan Allen and Josh Downs, so both passing games come with questions.

Pittsburgh Steelers at Cincinnati Bengals, Sunday Night Football

Everyone is talking about the Bengals as Super Bowl contenders, myself included, and this pick doesn’t change my mind. I’m simply fading public perception. If Cincinnati is a true Super Bowl contender, why is it only a 3½-point favorite at home in a massive primetime showdown with the Paycor Stadium crowd ready to rock? It seems like the books know something we don’t.

I’m not a huge believer in Pittsburgh, but the Steelers typically play the Bengals well. Using Bet Legend Pro’s historical lines, Cincinnati is 5-10 against the spread against Pittsburgh under Zac Taylor, including 2-5 as a favorite and 1-2 as a home favorite. The Bengals are also 1-6 ATS in the matchup since 2023.

That’s enough for me to think Pittsburgh keeps this AFC North showdown within a field goal.

We’re on the same side here. Pittsburgh won the first meeting and comes off a bye while Cincinnati returns from Madrid. The Steelers can lean on the run and keep Joe Burrow off the field. Burrow’s success against zone gives Cincinnati a good chance to win, which is exactly why I want the hook. A Bengals field-goal win cashes for both of us.

For full transparency, I used GPT-6.1 Sol with the thinking effort set to ultra. I supplied the odds board captured Thursday at noon ET and gave it the following prompt:

"Pick your five best bets for Week 10 based on the odds provided. No bet can be priced worse than -120. Review every spread, total and moneyline that falls within those parameters and determine whether it belongs among your five picks. Explain exactly why you’re selecting each of the five bets. Also explain exactly why you’re passing on the eligible bets you don’t select. Use at least 10 different sources for each game so you have a broad understanding of everything surrounding each game. Before delivering the results, do a fact-check and ensure that everything is correct."

Kansas City Chiefs at Atlanta Falcons, Sunday at 1 p.m. ET

Atlanta’s offense runs through Bijan Robinson, and Kansas City has the run defense to keep him from dictating the game. That puts more on Michael Penix Jr. against a defense allowing 17.9 points per game. Patrick Mahomes practiced fully Wednesday after hurting his elbow, and Atlanta just traded safety Jessie Bates III.

GPT likes Patrick Mahomes and Kenneth Walker to help the Chiefs score enough points to cover on the road against the Atlanta Falcons. (Getty Images)

The Falcons can get pressure, so Mahomes’ elbow is worth watching. At even money, I’m willing to lay the extra half-point because Kansas City has the better matchup on both sides of the ball.

GPT’s projected score: Chiefs 26, Falcons 20

Kansas City has a massive advantage at both head coach and quarterback, but I'm wary of laying three points and the hook with the Chiefs as a road favorite in a game where the public also figures to want to hammer the Chiefs.

Minnesota Vikings at Green Bay Packers, Sunday at 1 p.m. ET

Minnesota has scored 16, 15 and six points in its last three games. Its defense still leads the NFL at 14.5 points allowed per game. If Kirk Cousins starts, he’ll have only a few days to get reacquainted with the offense after Tuesday’s trade. Green Bay also expects to be without Josh Jacobs after he fractured a finger.

Jordan Love just threw for 372 yards, and the first meeting produced 61 points. I’m still taking the under because Minnesota can make things harder on Love and has struggled to finish drives of its own.

GPT’s projected score: Packers 21, Vikings 17

NFL TRADE DEADLINE WINNERS AND LOSERS, INCLUDING DIANNA RUSSINI AND KIRK COUSINS

I like this pick. With the Packers coming off a 45-point explosion against the Patriots, this is the perfect time to fade what we saw most recently. The Vikings defense is legit and Minnesota figures to be relatively conservative on offense with Kirk Cousins making his 2026 debut for the team.

Buffalo Bills at New York Jets, Sunday at 1 p.m. ET

Buffalo leads the NFL at 32 points per game, and James Cook gets a Jets defense that has allowed more than 140 rushing yards per game over its last four. The Jets settled for four field goals against Kansas City last week. That’s a problem if Josh Allen and Cook build an early lead.

Josh Allen is a stud, but 8 points is a lot to lay on the road against a divisional matchup. (Matt Krohn-Imagn Images)

Buffalo is on a short week and has injuries up front, so there’s some risk in laying eight on the road. I’ll take the matchup, with a push if the Bills win by exactly eight.

Betting against the Bills bit me last week, so this was an easy pass for me. Obviously, Buffalo deserves to be a heavy favorite, but I couldn't bring myself to lay this many points on the road in a divisional game.

San Francisco 49ers at Dallas Cowboys, Sunday at 4:25 p.m. ET

Both offenses rank in the top six in scoring, so I understand why the total is this high. I’m counting on San Francisco’s defense to keep Dallas from doing its share. The 49ers allow 19.5 points per game, and the Cowboys lost tight end Jake Ferguson to a knee injury.

San Francisco could score in the 30s against this Dallas defense. That’s the biggest risk, but 56½ gives us room for both teams to score. The 49ers can put up 31 and Dallas can score 24 and the under still cashes.

GPT’s projected score: 49ers 30, Cowboys 24

I like this pick from a pure numbers standpoint because 56½ points is a ton for an NFL game. In fact, if the number closes here, it would be the highest total in the league this season. Both teams can score, obviously, but when a game can finish 30-24 and still hit the under, I'd rather be on that side.

Pittsburgh Steelers at Cincinnati Bengals, Sunday Night Football

Pittsburgh won the first meeting 30-27 and comes off a bye while Cincinnati returns from Madrid. The Steelers allow 18 points per game and have a favorable rushing matchup that can help keep Joe Burrow on the sideline.

Burrow is the reason I want the hook. He completes a league-best 74.7% of his passes against zone, and Pittsburgh plays zone on more than 84% of opposing dropbacks. Cincinnati can win that matchup and take the game by a field goal. Pittsburgh +3½ still cashes.

GPT’s projected score: Bengals 24, Steelers 21
