title: Washington DC shooting: suspect confirmed dead after one person is killed and four injured – latest updates
excerpt:
Suspect has died after suffering a gunshot wound; one injured person in critical condition

Multiple people shot in Washington DC as police warn people to stay inside

In an update from police, the su...
body_text:
Suspect has died after suffering a gunshot wound; one injured person in critical condition

Multiple people shot in Washington DC as police warn people to stay inside

In an update from police, the suspect is confirmed to have been pronounced dead on the scene.

The shelter-in-place has also been lifted.

Per the social media update, “Traffic update: 14th Street, NW, in both directions is open. MPD is still asking the public to avoid the area while the investigation continues.”

Speaking to NBC Washington, Ward 2 council member and local resident Brooke Pinto said that preliminary information appears to reveal that the shooter was targeting someone in the gym “that he had been in active litigation with over a condo issue.”

“It’s just so sad and so senseless to kill someone over a dispute that should be worked out reasonably,” Pinto said, adding that the shooting “doesn’t appear to be as targeted as the initial shooting inside of VIDA [Fitness],” she added.

Pinto further said that the building has some damage because the suspect had allegedly set parts of it on fire.

Large numbers of police in tactical gear arrived in downtown Washington DC where an active shooter incident “resulted in a barricade situation in the 1500 block of 15th Street, Northwest”, the DC police said.

Four people are injured and one is dead, with the suspect also being pronounced deceased at the scene.

In an update from police, the suspect is confirmed to have been pronounced dead on the scene.

The shelter-in-place has also been lifted.

Per the social media update, “Traffic update: 14th Street, NW, in both directions is open. MPD is still asking the public to avoid the area while the investigation continues.”

A witness to the deadly shooting at the DC gym this morning tells the Guardian he walked toward a loud bang and found a man lying dead on the floor, with blood nearby, before being evacuated past the body and hearing about five more gunshots outside.

Anthony Mirones, 23, had gone to Vida Fitness after a run and about five minutes after arriving, he went to the cardio area and got on a treadmill. At around 8am, he heard the first bang.

“Everyone’s confused. I’m confused,” Mirones said. “Did the painting fall? Did something even worse fall?”

He went toward the noise and saw someone on the ground. A person standing closer to the body looked back and told him the man was dead.

“So I come a little closer and I see body on floor, some blood,” Mirones said. “I’m thinking about the loud bangs. I’m like, gunshot.”

He says a woman tried to give first aid but stopped almost immediately. Mirones believed the wound was to the upper body, near the neck.

A gym employee came over, saw what had happened, and then the fire alarm went off, and everyone began to evacuate.

“Everyone evacuates, so we all evacuate eventually,” Mirones said. “The thing is, people who are in the cardio area kind of have to step over the body to exit.”

Outside, at the entrance, police officers rushed in. “One police officer unholsters his gun, and then another police officer is asking for a description of the assailant,” Mirones said. “While this guy is describing the assailant, we hear five or so gunshots, and then we just all scatter and run.”

In an update shared on social media, DC police have said:

double quotation markThe barricade has concluded. The scene is safe. Significant traffic closures remain in place. MPD is still asking the public to avoid the area.

In another update on the thread, residents impacted by the shooting are told to check in at the Stead Park Recreation Center (1625 P St NW).

According to multiple reports, the suspect has died.

The death was confirmed to the Associated Press by a law enforcement official, who was not authorized to publicly discuss the ongoing investigation into what happened and spoke on the condition of anonymity.

CNN, NBC News and BBC News hear the same, citing law enforcement sources.

These are from my colleague Joseph Gedeon ahead of the news conference a short while ago.

Vida Fitness has posted a story on Instagram informing members that its Logan Circle location is closed “until further notice” following the shooting.

“The safety and well-being of our members, guests, and team are our highest priorities. We ask that you avoid traveling to the Logan Circle location and surrounding area until further notice. If you are currently in the vicinity, please follow all instructions from local law enforcement,” the post said.

DC mayor Muriel Bowser told the news conference that this was “a senseless act of gun violence”, and that “this lone gunman has been contained”. She also confirmed the White House had been briefed.

The suspect had a handgun “at one point in time”, but police “don’t know if there’s other weapons that are involved”, Carroll said. The suspect was also a member of the gym.

Officers said they believe the suspect barricaded himself into his own apartment and that he shot at officers more than once.

“He did fire through the door at officers at least on two occasions while he was barricaded inside,” Carroll said.

The exact timeline and locations are still to be determined, but the first shooting was reported inside the gym; the exact motivation is still is also yet to be determined.

Police said they believe they “have an idea” who the suspect is and that he had “some sort of conflict with the apartment building”.

“We do know there was a conflict between him and the homeowners association of that building, but at this point we’re continuing to look into that,” Carroll said.

Carroll said that the suspect had barricaded himself in a unit on the seventh floor of the building, which they believe was his own.

Negotiators made contact with the suspect and had been talking to him for an hour over the phone, Carroll said. Officers later heard a gunshot and the suspect stopped communicating with them; they forced entry, and found the suspect suffering from what appears to be a self-inflicted gunshot wound.

Emergency services have since been rendered, and his status has not been confirmed, Carroll added.

Police are looking into everything and Carroll emphasized that they are “very early in the investigation”.

He added that they believe there was a fire at some point inside the building, and that it has been put out and contained.

Police discovered the suspect, a white male, with a gunshot wound in a nearby apartment building from where the initial shooting occurred, Carroll said. The suspect is “contained”, he added.

Police in Washington DC have confirmed one person has been killed in this morning’s shooting and four injured.

“At this time, we have located a total of four individuals that were shot here on the scene, and one individual who is deceased,” Jeffery W Carroll, the interim chief of the Metropolitan Police Department, told a news conference.

Of the four surviving, one is in critical condition and the others do not have life-threatening injuries, he said.

He also said emergency services got a call just before 8am to report a shooting, and were on the scene “within 30 seconds”.

Further to that, NBC News reports that the suspect is barricaded in an apartment building above the gym on 15th Street, citing a federal law enforcement official.

title: Howard Lutnick is next Trump official top Dems want on the chopping block amid NVIDIA scandal
excerpt:
Congressional Democrats tell Fox News Digital that members of the administration, including Lutnick, Rubio, Homan and Miller could be on their chopping block in the 120th Congress

EXCLUSIVE : Top Hou...
body_text:
Congressional Democrats tell Fox News Digital that members of the administration, including Lutnick, Rubio, Homan and Miller could be on their chopping block in the 120th Congress

EXCLUSIVE : Top House Democrats are calling for an investigation into Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick over allegations involving NVIDIA's former CEO's reported relationship with an alleged Chinese spy.

NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang resigned this week following allegations that he had an affair with Alice Huang, an executive at Singapore-based Megaspeed who is suspected of being a Chinese spy.

In the midst of the spy scandal, multiple investigative reports emerged claiming Lutnick received a classified memo warning him about Huang’s relationship with alleged Chinese spy Alice Huang, of no familial relation to the NVIDIA CEO.

"Howard Lutnick needs to be investigated over his role in Jensen Huang and the Chinese spy, we're going to have an investigation into those allegations, that's completely unacceptable," Rep. Ted Lieu, D-Calif., who is expected to become chairman of the House Democratic Caucus, told Fox News Digital.

FOREIGN SPY ‘HONEYTRAPS’ TARGETING AMERICA’S TECH ELITE SPARK ALARM AMID NVIDIA CEO SCANDAL

Howard Lutnick joined the Trump administration as Commerce Secretary in 2025 after co-chairing Trump’s transition team. (Aaron Schwartz/CNP/Bloomberg via Getty Images)

Lieu alleged that despite Lutnick being briefed on the reported relationship between Huang and a woman identified by U.S. intelligence as a Chinese spy, he failed to take action.

Rep. Ro Khanna, D-Calif., a vice chair of the Congressional Progressive Caucus and member of the House Select Committee on China, also expressed support for investigating Lutnick and did not rule out examining Secretary of State Marco Rubio's involvement, as well.

"I think we need transparency," Khanna told Fox News Digital. "I think we need to understand what they knew."

PROGRESSIVE GROUP'S 182-PAGE BLUEPRINT MAPS OUT POTENTIAL DEM INVESTIGATIONS INTO TRUMP, CORPORATE ALLIES

"Rubio knew about the Chinese spy, and then got invited to the China trip," Khanna continued. "We need to get to the bottom of this."

Lutnick and Rubio did not respond to Fox News Digital’s request for comment.

(L-R) US Secretary of the Interior Doug Burgum, US Secretary of State Marco Rubio, US President Donald Trump, US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth and US Secretary of Commerce Howard Lutnick listen, during a cabinet meeting, in the Cabinet Room of the White House in Washington, DC, of April 30, 2025. (JIM WATSON/AFP via Getty Images)

REBECCA GRANT: JENSEN HUANG OWES AMERICA AN APOLOGY, AND NVIDIA OWES INVESTORS ANSWERS

Many left-leaning lawmakers are jumping on the chance to name the Cabinet official they want to see face scrutiny when Democrats take back control of the House in January.

However, neither Khanna or Lieu shed light on how they would investigate, prosecute or remove Lutnick, and potentially Rubio. Neither of the Cabinet secretaries have been formally accused or indicted of wrongdoing in connection with the NVIDIA case.

House Minority Leader Rep. Hakeem Jeffries, D-N.Y., who is currently running unopposed for the Democratic nomination for Speaker of the House, did not respond to Fox News Digital’s request for comment on whether he spoke to either lawmakers on their desires to take action against Lutnick and Rubio.

HAKEEM JEFFRIES DECLARES BID FOR HOUSE SPEAKER AFTER GOP'S MIDTERM MASSACRE

The lawmakers' remarks signal that congressional Democrats could use their incoming majority to investigate senior Trump administration officials over their handling of alleged Chinese intelligence threats.

Rep. Ro Khanna (D-CA) appears on "Meet the Press" in Washington D.C., Sunday, Sep. 1, 2024 (William B. Plowman/NBC via Getty Images)

It is unclear whether Republican lawmakers will support the Democrats' investigations. But following Huang’s resignation, House Select Committee on China Chairman John Moolenaar, R-Mich., announced that the outgoing CEO has agreed to brief congressional committees following the scandal.

He also advocated for Congress to act quickly to pass bipartisan export control legislation in the year-end national defense bill.

Moolenaar welcomed the resignation and added that companies such as NVIDIA should "never jeopardize our nation’s security by giving Chinese companies access to their most advanced chips," and called on them to "change its corporate practices and appoint leadership that makes national security its top priority."

title: Best hiking spots in Eugene, Oregon, ahead of the Ducks' showdown with the Michigan Wolverines
excerpt: NASCAR driver Chase Briscoe joins OutKick OutDoors to explain how he developed a love for hunting and the outdoors, how his young son Brooks got involved, and why getting his kids away from screens an...
body_text:
NASCAR driver Chase Briscoe joins OutKick OutDoors to explain how he developed a love for hunting and the outdoors, how his young son Brooks got involved, and why getting his kids away from screens and outside matters to him.

Trying to find a good city for both incredible hiking spots and some elite college football? Then Eugene, Oregon, has to be near the top of your list.

Sure, the Ducks have sputtered a bit this season, but they are still in the thick of a College Football Playoff race, especially if they win out.

This page may contain affiliate links to legal sports betting partners. If you sign up or place a wager, FOX News may be compensated. This content was created by a team that works independently from the FOX newsroom.

The Oregon Ducks mascot dances to "shout" at the end of the third quarter a game between the Oregon Ducks and the Montana State Bobcats at Autzen Stadium on Aug. 30, 2025 in Eugene, Oregon. (Tom Hauck/Getty Images)

They take on the Michigan Wolverines this weekend in Eugene, which means you have an excuse to make your way to one of the most scenic campuses in the country.

The entire Pacific Northwest is breathtaking, and this week, we will identify a handful of the best hikes the Beaver State has to offer.

Western red cedars stand on a ridge at Spencer Butte in Oregon. (UCG/Universal Images Group via Getty Images)

Perhaps the best all-around spot for a hike in the Eugene area (and that's saying something), Spencer Butte can offer a bird's-eye view of the surrounding locale before heading to Autzen Stadium for the game.

The 2,058-foot peak is the highest point in Eugene's Ridgeline park system and will give hikers a panoramic view of both the Cascade Mountains and Coast Range.

If you're looking for a challenge, try the West Trail, which offers a more demanding alternative, with scrambling and slippery rocks in wet weather.

Any serious hiker has to put Spencer Butte at the top of their list, and the views alone are worth the trek.

New Year's sunrise illuminates the Kesey Memorial at the summit of Mount Pisgah in the Howard Buford Recreation Area in Eugene, Ore. Created by sculptor Pete Melzer, the memorial has slots oriented to catch the winter and summer solstices. (Universal Images Group via Getty Images)

If Spencer Butte is the most iconic summit in Eugene, Mount Pigsah is a close second.

Offering over 30 miles of trails throughout the Howard Buford Recreation Center, Mount Pigsah features a 1,518-foot peak surrounded by more than 2,200 acres of oak savanna, meadows, riverside habitat and wooded slopes.

WATCH: YOUNG BEAR TAKES ROUGH TUMBLE FROM DENVER TREE AFTER WILDLIFE OFFICERS TRANQUILIZE IT

Hikers looking for a more strenuous adventure will definitely want to check the summit out, while those looking for a more leisurely stroll should stick to the Arboretum.

That's the beauty of Mount Pigsah, there's something here for everyone.

This is one of Western Oregon's best mountain views and it's just a few miles from campus.

You couldn't ask for much more than that.

Our first two entries were a bit on the more rugged and elevated side, but if you're looking to be one with nature while taking things a bit slower, try Hendricks Park.

Located just minutes from campus, the park allows you to walk among Douglas firs that are over 200 years old.

University of Oregon's campus located in Eugene, Oregon. (Marli Miller/UCG/Universal Images Group via Getty Images)

It's one of Eugene's oldest parks, and the whole complex spans over 80 acres of gardens and forest.

THE BEST HIKING AND OUTDOOR SPOTS NEAR FOLSOM FIELD FOR TEXAS TECH AT COLORADO GAME WEEKEND

Hendricks Park offers a convenient and relaxing gameday hike that won't require a day trip, as you get to experience some of the emerald beauty of the Pacific Northwest without having to leave the zip code you're staying in.

A hidden gem that offers incredible wide open prairie vibes, Wild Iris Ridge Park will have you questioning whether you're in Oregon or rural England.

The trail offers a departure from some of the dense forests and buttes we've discussed so far, but that doesn't mean there isn't plenty of beauty to be seen.

The park is home to over 250 acres of upland prairie and oak habitats that give way to views of the aforementioned Spencer Butte and the West Eugene Wetlands.

The rolling hills are a sight to behold, especially with fall foliage, and the preserve is particularly interesting for anyone who enjoys birdwatching or native plant habitats.

It's one of the lesser-known hiking destinations on the list, but the change of scenery and lack of tourists should be something that might pique your interest.

Consider this a bit of a bonus pick, since you'll need a full day to make it out here (but the trip is worth it).

Roughly an hour and a half from campus sits Salt Creek Falls, which offers spectacular waterfall views poking through dense forests.

At 286 feet, Salt Creek is the second-highest waterfall in Oregon, meaning one of the state's most breathtaking views is within driving distance for any college football fan staying the weekend in town.

The observation platform is a stone's throw from the parking lot, and the additional trails offer other vantage points as well as a connection to neighboring Diamond Creek Falls.

It's a drive, as I've noted before, but the facilities close in the winter, so if you have the time this weekend, I highly recommend making a stop out here.

title: Trump opens door to immigration deal, but Republicans have one condition
excerpt: "Obama did this very thing. They still call him the 'deporter in chief'. And he did oversee a lot of deportations. But those numbers were also cooked. The books were cooked because they were counting ...
body_text:
"Obama did this very thing. They still call him the 'deporter in chief'. And he did oversee a lot of deportations. But those numbers were also cooked. The books were cooked because they were counting things as deportations that were, in fact, just turnaways at the border and many other things baked into those Obama numbers. But then what he did when he tried to push his Dreamers and all his things, and he said, look, I've deported all these people. I've done what you wanted with that. Now we need to start looking at amnesty and legal status. But this is the exact same thing that we're seeing today.

Some Senate Republicans are open to revisiting immigration policy after President Donald Trump floated a possible deal with Democrats, but they insist amnesty remains off the table.

Republicans, after sweeping midterm losses, are willing to open up the immigration policy debate after voters made clear that they didn't support the administration’s approach: a Fox News poll published in September found that 53% of voters believed that Trump's immigration policy had gone too far.

But there’s one thing that Senate Republicans won’t agree to: amnesty.

WHITE HOUSE DOUBLES DOWN AFTER TRUMP ANGERS BASE BY FLOATING ILLEGAL ALIEN DEAL WITH DEMS

President Donald Trump arrives to deliver remarks during a campaign rally at the Rock Hill Sports and Event Center in Rock Hill, S.C., on Oct. 29, 2026. Trump was in South Carolina rallying support for local Republican candidates ahead of the midterm elections. (Getty Images)

"I trust President Trump," Sen. Jim Banks, R-Ind., told Fox News Digital. "He's gonna do what's right, but as far as I'm concerned, amnesty is off the table. I'll never go for it."

The door creaked open on the idea when Trump, during an interview with "60 Minutes" that aired over the weekend, said that his administration’s mass deportation and enforcement policies might be "too tough."

"Get the killers out, get the rapists out, get all the rough ones out, get the drug dealers out," Trump said. "But let the people that are here — and in some cases here for 10 and 15 years — work a deal for them."

The administration quickly sought to clarify Trump’s comments, with Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin affirming that there would be "no amnesty" shortly after.

HOUSE GOP ERUPTS AT STEPHEN MILLER AS TRUMP ELEVATES HIM AFTER MIDTERM MASSACRE: 'MEGALOMANIAC'

Still, Republicans are willing to navigate the complex issue as Democrats gear up to take power next year. Some have been calling for action on the matter for months.

Sen. Thom Tillis, R-N.C., one of the administration’s sharper Republican critics on immigration policy who is retiring at the end of the year, told Fox News Digital that as early as March he texted Trump and suggested it would be the "perfect time" to codify "all the stuff that has effectively sealed the border and used it as an opportunity to get merit-based immigration reform."

"I also said in that text, though, was, in order for this to be successful, Stephen Miller either needs to be out of the room or on his meds," Tillis said. "And so he's the reason they're walking it back is because they don't want to do it, because they have some false assumption that that's gonna hurt our base."

"Our base is fine with merit-based immigration reform. President Trump is fine with merit-based immigration reform," he continued. "And if we don't get the stuff codified that has effectively sealed the border, it's gonna be on them when the border gets opened up if a Democrat wins in ‘28."

The Senate, just before Trump won the 2024 election, was on the cusp of a bipartisan immigration deal when Democrats controlled the chamber. The deal collapsed after Trump criticized it and Senate Republicans withdrew support.

"There's a lot of scar tissue on this issue, but, you know, the president, because he secured the borders, he has credibility on the issue, and he has expressed a willingness," Senate Majority Leader John Thune, R-S.D., said. "I have not seen anything yet that's being proposed, but we will certainly hear them out, and if there's something he wants to do there, have a conversation about it."

JEFFRIES VOWS DEMOCRATS WON’T ‘GIVE A DIME’ TO TRUMP’S DEPORTATION EFFORTS

Sen. James Lankford, R-Okla., accused Senate Democrats of being more afraid of "ICE than they are of Iran." (Allison Robbert/Bloomberg via Getty Images)

The bipartisan deal was the product of negotiations among Sens. James Lankford, R-Okla., Chris Murphy, D-Conn., and former Sen. Kyrsten Sinema, and would have funneled billions for border security and shuttered the border to most asylum seekers, among several other policy changes. But conservatives balked at the deal, and Trump’s influence from the campaign trail ultimately killed it.

Years later, Lankford is again in a prime position to work on a deal with Democrats, given that he is expected to become the ranking Republican on the Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs Committee next year.

"If I’m ranking on Homeland Security, I’m right in the thick of it, whether you like it or not," Lankford said.

Though opinions vary on what exactly the GOP’s approach would be going forward, many Republicans agree that the administration’s enforcement policies, particularly under former Homeland Security Secretary Kristi Noem, should not make a comeback.

"I think you have to make sure, first and foremost, that how you do your enforcement is not like the administration started under Kristi Noem," Sen. Ted Budd, R-N.C., told Fox News Digital.

"I think people are for some enforcement, but not in a cruel way. And there were so many, there was a lack of training, lack of proper methodologies, and I think people want to take enforcement seriously."

"But, again, I would say no amnesty at all," he continued. "We don't want to go there. Ronald Reagan, a great president, one of his few regrets, but significant regrets, was amnesty. And I don't think Trump wants to make that mistake."

Alex Miller is a writer for Fox News Digital covering the U.S. Senate.

title: Sadiq Khan joins Labour figures urging PM not to water down electric vehicle targets – UK politics live
excerpt:
The mayor of London is the most high-profile figure to weigh into the debate over electric vehicle targets

Kiran Stacey is the Guardian’s policy editor.

Sadiq Khan has become the most high-profile L...
body_text:
The mayor of London is the most high-profile figure to weigh into the debate over electric vehicle targets

Kiran Stacey is the Guardian’s policy editor.

Sadiq Khan has become the most high-profile Labour figure to weigh into the increasingly fractious debate over what the government should do with its electric vehicle targets.

Ministers are meeting today in Downing Street to decide whether to cut legally binding requirements for carmakers to ensure 80% of the vehicles they sell in 2030 are electric.

Jonathan Reynolds, the business secretary, is pushing for the target to be reduced to 50%, but Miatta Fahnbulleh, the energy secretary, wants to keep it as close to 80% as possible.

But as ministers wrangle among each other, City Hall officials have made clear that the London mayor is on Fahnbulleh’s side.
 
 
 Khan’s position was laid out in a letter from his deputy mayor for transport Seb Dance to Oliver Lord, the UK director of Clean Cities, which has been seen by the Guardian.

double quotation markWe and Transport for London share your view that the ZEV [zero-emission vehicle] mandate must not change. We outlined in our submission to the government’s consultation that London supports a strong and credible ZEV mandate.

We do not support any weakening of the current trajectories to 2030 or beyond, which risks damaging the case for investment in the ZEV and charging infrastructure industries, slowing down the pace of change, and the associated reduction in harmful emissions.

Department for Transport officials insist that no decision has yet been made but with the government likely to announce a cut to the 2030 target in the next two
 
 weeks, this is likely to leave Khan opposed to official government policy.

Some young people with disabilities will lose their personal independence payments and will have to apply instead to a local fund for short-term expenses and equipment, Alan Milburn’s review will recommend.

Andy Burnham said he and Ursula von der Leyen would use their meeting in Dublin to work to get a deal “over the line” for next week’s UK-EU summit. As the Press Association reports, the PM met the European Commission president at the European Political Community summit today, and they will see each other again in Brussels to sign agreements on food and farming, emissions trading and a youth mobility scheme. Burnham said at the start of the bilateral meeting:

double quotation markObviously, we have a UK-EU summit seven days away now, a week tomorrow, and our teams – who are working very well – and we’re really grateful to you and your colleagues.

We have potentially a deal that can be good for businesses in the UK in terms of cutting red tape, reducing costs on business, but also good for consumers as well in terms of lowering prices. Good for young people potentially.

But we’ve got to try and get this deal over the line, and that’s what today is about.

Sadiq Khan has become the most high-profile Labour figure to weigh into the increasingly fractious debate over what the government should do with its electric vehicle targets. (See 1.54pm.)

Nigel Farage appeared on Russell Brand’s US podcast nine months after the comedian was investigated by police over allegations of sexual assault, the Guardian has learned.

The UK government has appointed the world’s first special representative for climate security, in the strongest sign yet of fears that climate breakdown will bring chaos to the country.

For a full list of all the stories covered on the blog today, do scroll through the list of key event headlines near the top of the blog.

Ed Balls has said that he warned Ed Miliband not to do an interview with Russell Brand during the 2015 election campaign. Miliband was Labour leader at the time, Balls shadow chancellor, and the interview – which was controversial at the time – was quoted by Kemi Badenoch this week in the light of Brand’s conviction for rape as evidence of Miliband’s flawed judgment.

Speaking on his Political Currency podcast, Balls said he had a dim view of Brand at the time of the interview.

double quotation markI actually only met him once in the green room on the Andrew Marr programme [...] he behaved really weirdly and was sort of trying to come up and kind of prod me and get in my face and I was concentrating on my interview and never engaged.

Balls said Brand had also insulted him during a Channel 4 show.

Describing what happened when he found out that Miliband was going to do an election interview with him, Balls said:

double quotation markAt the time, the feedback from my office back to them was what are you doing with this guy? I mean, he’s weird, and he’s untrustworthy, and he’s already been removed from the BBC for his behaviour. And do we really want this?

But they decided to go ahead because they thought it would solve a political problem.

I ended up having to go on the television, in which I have to defend this because I’m the shadow chancellor. So I say, well, you know, I guess they think it will connect with the young people, and so be it.

But, although he defended the move in public, privately he thought doing the interview was “ridiculous”, he said.

Reform UK is seen as a rightwing party. But that does not mean it is automatically pro-business. In his speech this afternoon, at a rally where the party unveiled its “industrial strongholds” policy (a revamped version of enterprize zones), Robert Jenrick, the party’s Treasury spokesperson, launched a strong attack on the owners of Poundland.

A father and a son. A market stall in this city. One shop by 1990. Six hundred shops today, and twelve thousand people on the payroll.

That is the Black Country story. Start small. Work hard. Build something that lasts.

It was sold abroad. Then it was sold again, to an American corporate raider, for a pound. The whole company. For a pound. They don’t even sell the products for that anymore.

Poundland is on course to make eighteen million quid in profit this year. Yet, its owners have filed for administration, despite buyers at the door offering to keep it whole. Why? So they can sell it off for parts and fat fees.

Think about that. A business that makes money. That employs twelve thousand people. That sells what families can actually afford. And the system’s answer is: break it up.

That isn’t capitalism. These aren’t titans of industry. They’re shysters.

These people are organ harvesters masquerading as doctors.

They don’t want the patient to live. They want him on the table, still warm, so they can sell him off a piece at a time.

Capitalism is the father and the son on the stall. This is something else. A model where it pays better to strip a British business than to build one.

Alan Milburn says in his Times interview today that he thinks it is worth cutting benefits to young people because the long-term advantages of getting them into work outweigh potential short-term financial disadvantages they will face. (See 12.44pm.)

The Joseph Rowntree Foundation, which campaigns to reduce poverty, disagrees. Responding to the Milburn interview, Iain Porter, a senior policy at the JRF, said:

double quotation markCutting someone’s income when they’re already struggling to afford food or the bus to college makes it harder for them to stay in education or find work.

The government can and should invest in supporting people back into employment. Young disabled people shouldn’t have to trade financial security for better employment support. They need both.

Young people with disabilities will lose their personal independence payments and will have to apply instead to a local fund for short-term expenses and equipment, Alan Milburn’s review will recommend. Jessica Elgot has the story.

Andy Burnham has promised Volodymyr Zelenskyy his “complete support” in the latest efforts to end the Ukraine war and said he would push for European representation in the US-brokered talks, the Press Association reports.

The PM co-chaired a group meeting on Ukraine with the country’s president at the European Political Community (EPC) summit in Ireland this afternoon.

Burnham was using the Dublin gathering to urge leaders from some 50 nations to ramp up pressure on Vladimir Putin to take peace talks seriously.

Speaking at the start of the meeting when journalists were present, Burnham said:

double quotation markI’m sure I speak for everybody in saying you have our complete support, both in terms of resisting the aggression that you continue to face, but also in the negotiation process that has started.

He added that allies will try to support Ukraine “in every way possible through that process”, and “we will obviously continue to press for European representation in that process”.

Burnham and Zelenskyy sat side by side at the head of the table at the meeting attended by more than a dozen leaders, including France’s Emmanuel Macron, Germany’s Friedrich Merz, Ireland’s Micheál Martin and Canada’s Mark Carney, as well as the presidents of the EU Commission and Council and the chief of Nato.

The latest episode of the Guardian’s Politics Weekly UK is out, and it features Kiran Stacey and Jessica Elgot discussing some of the concerns starting to be raised by Labour MPs about Andy Burnham’s policies.

Ben Quinn is a Guardian political correspondent.

Reform UK has pledged to create “industrial strongholds” that would get tax breaks and other incentives aimed at spurring reindustrialisation, with the Black Country identified by the party as the first area for one.

The West Midlands area encompassing Wolverhampton, Dudley, Sandwell, Walsall and Cannock Chase – all Reform UK targets in any upcoming general election – was identified by the party as its first proposed “stronghold” zone.

Each zone would be a place where employer national insurance on net new hires would be halved, along with “streamlining” of planning policy and 100% first-year tax relief on new brownfield residential buildings and extensions.

Four more areas are to be unveiled by Reform UK in the months ahead, a rally in Wolverhampton was told by Reform’s economics spokesperson, Robert Jenrick.

Gordon Brown’s controversial 2007 pledge to create “British jobs for British workers” was also repurposed by Jenrick in a speech in which he spoke of plans for new visa sponsorship rules. He said:

double quotation markUnder Reform, jobs in Britain go to British workers first. Advertised here, to our people, before an employer can look anywhere else. And no sitting out the clock to fly somebody in on a visa.

Cheaper to hire from Bilston. Dearer to hire from abroad. British jobs for British workers. It’s about time you came first.

In a briefing explaining how the policy would work, Reform UK said:

double quotation markEach Industrial Stronghold will be a defined geographical area, within which businesses will benefit from significant incentives for growth. These will include:

-Employer national insurance contributions reduced by 50% for the first £50,000 of earnings for net additional employees for five years.

-100% first-year tax relief on new brownfield residential buildings, extensions and substantial improvements.

-10-year exemptions on the extra business rates that result from new investment, from improvements, and from establishing a business in a high street retail unit that has been vacant for more than two years.

-Streamlining planning policy by creating a presumption in favour of development according to an updated local plan, with a strictly limited set of circumstances in which planning applications can be refused.

Andy Burnham said he had been “really looking forward” to meeting Italian premier Giorgia Meloni for the first time face to face, the Press Association reports. PA says:

double quotation markThe pair highlighted close UK-Italian ties and joint projects – including the Global Combat Air Programme (Gcap) to build the next generation fighter jet – as they met on the sidelines of the European Political Community summit in Dublin.

Speaking to the media ahead of private talks, the prime minister said: “It’s a real pleasure for me to meet the prime minister of Italy, Giorgia, for the first time.

“Italy, one of the UK’s biggest trading partners, we have such a close relationship on so many levels, not just trading partners, security partners, because working together on the next generation fighter jet Gcap.

“Working together closely on security, particularly on Ukraine, and we really salute your strong stance on Ukraine.”

Meloni told Mr Burnham “it’s a pleasure to know you personally”, and also referenced the two countries’ co-operation on migration.

EU relations minister Hamish Falconer and national security adviser Jonathan Powell also attended the meeting.

Nigel Farage appeared on Russell Brand’s US podcast nine months after the comedian was investigated by police over allegations of sexual assault, Rowena Mason reports.

title: Daniel Jones, Jonathan Taylor react to Colts fire sale as they remain put: 'You're not happy to see it'
excerpt: Kirk Cousins was traded from the Las Vegas Raiders to the Minnesota Vikings, and Fernando Mendoza will start Week 10 vs. the Seattle Seahawks. Nick Wright, Kevin Wildes, Danny Parkins, and Greg Jennin...
body_text:
Kirk Cousins was traded from the Las Vegas Raiders to the Minnesota Vikings, and Fernando Mendoza will start Week 10 vs. the Seattle Seahawks. Nick Wright, Kevin Wildes, Danny Parkins, and Greg Jennings discuss the expectations for the 1st-overall pick, and whether or not the Indianapolis Colts should’ve traded Jonathan Taylor.

The NFL trade deadline has come and gone, and the Indianapolis Colts are one of those teams without many key contributors from the beginning of the season after a fire sale amid a struggling campaign.

No, running back Jonathan Taylor wasn’t among them, as he stayed put in Indy. But players like wide receivers Keenan Allen and Josh Downs joined Quenton Nelson and DeForest Buckner as trade pieces to other teams.

This page may contain affiliate links to legal sports betting partners. If you sign up or place a wager, FOX News may be compensated. This content was created by a team that works independently from the FOX newsroom.

The Colts are clearly rebuilding, and quarterback Daniel Jones and running back Jonathan Taylor – both involved in trade rumors before Tuesday’s deadline -- still have to play eight games this season despite a depleted roster.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

Daniel Jones hands the ball to Jonathan Taylor against the Dallas Cowboys during the third quarter at Lucas Oil Stadium in Indianapolis, Ind., on Nov. 8, 2026. (Getty Images)

Jones admitted not being happy with selling off the pieces owner Carlie Irsay-Gordon and the front office did, but understands this is a business. He knows it, too, after what happened during his time with the New York Giants.

"Honestly, you’re not happy to see it, right?" he said on Wednesday while speaking with reporters. "You’re a player and you’re going out there competing and doing everything you can to win games. So, you’re not happy to see a lot of those decisions.

"But it’s outside of our control and our job is to play and be prepared to play well."

While talks that Jones could be on the move came later in the trade deadline period, Taylor was the biggest what-if across the league.

Indianapolis Colts quarterback Daniel Jones (17) runs off the field after the game against the Los Angeles Chargers at SoFi Stadium. The game was played in Inglewood, California, on Oct. 19, 2025. (Jayne Kamin-Oncea/Imagn Images)

When the Colts made it clear with the Nelson and Buckner deals that they would be selling assets with just two wins on the year, Taylor’s name was quickly added to the rumors and speculation. The Colts initially said they wouldn’t be accepting phone calls on a possible trade for him, but that tune changed.

Teams like the Giants and Denver Broncos came calling, but ultimately, the Colts decided to keep their elite running back in place as well as Jones.

"Those are some hard decisions that you have to make," Taylor, who even said farewell to Indianapolis and its fans just in case he was traded after losing to the Dallas Cowboys last week, said in his first comments since the trade deadline passed. "I’m glad I don’t have to make those decisions. I’m glad I just have to come in here, make sure I’m at my best every single day for my coaches and my teammates. So, I would hate to be in that situation.

"I know they have a vision and a plan for it, and right now, we gotta execute right now. The best thing that’s going to help us is executing, going out and getting a win against Miami."

Indianapolis Colts running back Jonathan Taylor takes off on a run Sunday, Oct. 18, 2026, during the game against the Tennessee Titans at Lucas Oil Stadium in Indianapolis. (USA TODAY Network)

OUTKICK IS NOW AVAILABLE ON THE FOX NEWS APP: CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD

All Jones and Taylor can do now is look ahead because they will be staying with the Colts for at least the remainder of the year. They both will likely lean on each other to get the offense going in the right direction for head coach Shane Steichen, but it’s going to be even harder now to correct the struggles.

Scott Thompson is a sports writer for Fox News Digital.

title: ‘I had the courage to believe in Mississippi’ says Scott Colom after historic Senate win – US politics live
excerpt:
Colom adds to blue wave of Democrat victories across the US and becomes Mississippi’s first black senator since 1875 after defeating Cindy Hyde-Smith

Hello, and welcome to the US politics live blog.
...
body_text:
Colom adds to blue wave of Democrat victories across the US and becomes Mississippi’s first black senator since 1875 after defeating Cindy Hyde-Smith

Hello, and welcome to the US politics live blog.

Mississippi has elected Scott Colom, a Democrat, as its senator, adding to a wave of Democratic gains across the country in this year’s midterm elections.

He defeated incumbent Republican Cindy Hyde-Smith in the closely contested Senate race to become the state’s first black senator since the post-Civil War Reconstruction era, marking a historic moment for Mississippi and a major breakthrough for the Democrats in a traditionally Republican state.

“All I did was have the courage to imagine a night like this,” Colom said in his victory speech last night.

“I had the courage to believe in Mississippi. I had the courage to understand that we can show the country that Mississippi matters.”

Just over a week since the midterm elections, the Associated Press called the race after absentee and provisional ballots were counted.

“While this is not the outcome we worked for or hoped for, I respect the decision of Mississippi voters,” Hyde-Smith said.

You can read more about Colom’s grassroots campaign, his viral advertising strategy and how he reached voters at Trump rallies despite limited early backing from national Democrats here:

US special envoy Steve Witkoff and Donald Trump’s son-in-law Jared Kushner have arrived in Moscow for talks with Vladimir Putin, seeking progress towards ending the war in Ukraine following negotiations with Russian and Ukrainian officials in Abu Dhabi.

US defence secretary Pete Hegseth was admonished by a military guard after he and his entourage were seen laughing and talking near the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier, where visitors are required to remain silent. The incident came days after Republicans blocked an attempt to impeach him.

Speaking of things Democrats want to investigate, Ukraine’s president Volodymyr Zelenskyy says Starlink, the satellite internet service his armed forces rely on to counter Russian drones, is once again unusably slow.

“We have detected speed restrictions on Starshield on our Ukrainian territory – in the temporarily occupied parts of Ukraine. The speed limit is back at 161 kilometers per hour – that’s 100 miles per hour,” Zelenskyy wrote on X earlier today.

“This directly affects our ability to intercept Russian jet-powered ‘shahed’ drones. These drones come from those areas, and because of the speed restrictions, we simply cannot catch up with them in time.”

Starlink is a project of Elon Musk, who Democrats will undoubtedly haul before Congress next year over an array of matters, including his leadership of the Department of Government Efficiency initiative that made widespread cuts to federal staffing and funding. Expect the Starlink throttling to come up at some point as well.

Here’s the latest on the conflict in Ukraine:

The Senate’s Democratic minority leader, Chuck Schumer, has called for an investigation both into former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s ties to an alleged Chinese spy, and the Trump administration’s handling of the matter.

The White House reportedly knew about Huang’s involvement with a woman said to be linked to Chinese intelligence, but still let him accompany Donald Trump on an official visit to China. Here’s what Schumer – who may be the Senate majority leader in about two months – had to say about all that:

double quotation markDespite Jensen Huang’s resignation, Congress must demand answers from Mr. Huang and others at Nvidia about how they may have put U.S. national security at risk.

The Trump administration must also answer for what it did once it learned about Mr. Huang’s relationship with a suspected Chinese intelligence asset. Were government officials told not to investigate because of Trump’s relationship with Mr. Huang? What did Trump know when he personally invited Mr. Huang aboard Air Force One?

Americans deserve to know that those at the highest levels of power are putting America first, not their bottom line or their personal friendships.

Pete Hegseth has issued a commendation to a US army sentinel who gave him and his entourage a reprimand yesterday, when the defense secretary visited the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier to mark Veterans Day.

On X, Hegseth posted pictures of him pinning a medal on to the guard’s uniform, and wrote:

The sentinel, who was not named, shouted at the secretary and those accompanying him when someone laughed during their visit to the tomb. Here’s more about the incident, which was captured by a TV camera:

As the Democratic House minority leader, Hakeem Jeffries is in line to become speaker when his party takes the majority in the chamber next year.

But it won’t be without controversy. Democrats have faced calls from activists and constituents to find another candidate, and a Change.org petition (started by someone who gets paid for such efforts) has received more than 1.15m signatures.

Asked about these tensions at his press conference, Jeffries issued a lengthy recap of his accomplishments while leading the party in the House during their soon-to-conclude period in the minority. He ended with:

double quotation markThe record speaks for itself. But that doesn’t mean it’s not important to talk to every single member of the House Democratic Caucus family about what the future looks like and how we can build upon this record where everyone doubted our ability to aggressively fight back and continue to bring about the type of bold, dramatic, and decisive change that the American people deserve.

Which is a pretty good sign that Jeffries has no intention of going anywhere next year but the speaker’s office.

For what it’s worth, Donald Trump thinks Apple CEO Tim Cook should take over as head of Nvidia.

“NOW THAT Nvidia CEO JENSEN HUANG, who has done a fantastic job, has resigned, there is only one man to take his place - TIM COOK of Apple. A Legend replaces a Legend!” the president wrote on Truth Social.

The Democratic House minority leader Hakeem Jeffries just said lawmakers should receive a classified briefing on the scandal surrounding chipmaker Nvidia.

The company is seen as among America’s most important, because it makes advanced chips that are powering the AI boom. Recently, it was revealed that its CEO, Jensen Huang, had an affair with a woman alleged to be a Chinese spy, leading to his resignation today.

“We need a classified briefing made available to members of Congress as it relates to the Nvidia situation and to the extent that our national security has been compromised,” Jeffries said at his ongoing press conference. “The American people deserve answers, and we’re going to work to make sure that happens.”

The Democratic House minority leader, Hakeem Jeffries, began his press conference today with a few words about the mass shooting in Washington DC.

“Our prayers and our thoughts certainly go out to anyone who has been victimized or hurt by this tragedy, all of the family members and loved ones,” said Jeffries, who is set to become speaker next year, when Democrats take the majority in the House.

“Our thanks go out to the Capitol Police, as well as of course the Metropolitan DC Police Department, and all of our law enforcement professionals [who] continue to work incredibly hard to keep the American people safe, and we’re grateful for their service, encourage their bravery, and their work.”

Here’s the latest on the shooting in the Logan Circle neighborhood:

Perhaps you saw this ad from Scott Colom, who was just elected to serve as Mississippi’s first Democratic senator since 1989:

The New York Times spoke to Russ Hudson, the man who is grilling in the first part of the ad and uttered the “sheeeit” that has now become an emblem of Colom’s successful campaign. Here’s what he had to say, from the Times:

double quotation markThe lines, he said, felt natural. He left thinking maybe a couple thousand people would see it.

“I just did it like a Mississippian would,” Mr. Hudson said in an interview.

Now, Mr. Hudson, an Army veteran who served in Afghanistan, has found himself as the unlikely face of one of the most potent campaign advertisements of the 2026 midterm cycle. The ad, released in the final weeks of the election season, became a defining feature of Mr. Colom’s campaign and his surge to a stunning upset.

“I never expected it to do what it did,” Mr. Hudson said.

He even downloaded TikTok to keep up with all the commentary his friends were sending him about the ad. Someone made him a “pick another protein” shirt with his face on it, along with the other two women in the ad.

And he keeps fielding requests to, well, say it again.

“They make me throw my head back with it, too,” he said.

There’s also much more to know about the downfall of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, who is close to Donald Trump.

We have another live blog covering the fallout from his resignation, and you can read it here:

We now have a separate live blog covering the latest on the shooting in Washington DC’s Logan Circle neighborhood.

An active shooter has reportedly barricaded himself after shooting at least five people in Washington DC near Logan Circle. Local police have put a notice out for a “white male, heavy built” wearing gray clothes. There is a shelter in place order for those in the immediate vicinity.

One local independent news outlet reported that the suspect has shot at police through the barricades.

Follow the Guardian’s reporting for more details.

double quotation markJensen Huang has resigned as President, Chief Executive Officer, and a member of the Board, effective immediately.

Huang is in the middle of a major geopolitical and corporate governance scandal after he admitted to extramarital affairs with an alleged Chinese intelligence asset.

The company added that current executive vice president and chief financial officer Collette Kress has agreed to serve as the interim CEO.

Continuing his Truth Social ranting, Donald Trump said he has asked the vice-president, JD Vance, to turn his “complete and total attention” to alleged corruption in Democratic-run cities and states, while also declaring that the US no longer needs a deal with Iran.

In the latest post this morning, Trump singled out Minnesota, California and Illinois as “poorly run, corrupt disasters” and claimed that “billions of dollars is being stolen each and every month”. He argued that the federal budget “could be quickly BALANCED” if what he called large-scale criminal activity were stopped, and said corruption was “in the Democrat Leadership’s blood”.

double quotation markCORRUPTION is in the Democrat Leadership’s blood! We don’t need a deal with Iran. Those days have long since passed. We’ve got their money, Hundreds of Billions of Dollars, and we’ve got their Strait!

He wasn’t done and followed up with another pile on posts minutes later:

double quotation markIf the Democrats want to “root out corruption,” they should start with investigating Blue States, perhaps the most CORRUPT governmental structures and entities anywhere on Earth. Big time money is being stolen each and every hour of the day!

In a further post on Truth Social, Trump renewed his criticism of Senate Republicans, warning that the party cannot afford to let legislation stall in Congress after suffering significant losses in the midterm elections.

He urged Republican senators to take a more aggressive approach to advancing his legislative agenda, arguing that the Senate must no longer be a place “where things are sent to die”.

He singled out the failure to pass the Save America Act, which would introduce stricter voter identification requirements and require proof of US citizenship when registering to vote. He described its failure to pass as “devastating” for Republicans in the midterms.

double quotation markAnyway, good luck to our Republican Senators, work hard, and congratulations to John Thune for another year of leadership, Minority though it may be!”

Trump has threatened to immediately double tariffs on Mexico unless the country stops migrant caravans travelling north towards the US.

The president issued the warning on Truth Social this morning, linking the renewed movement of people through Mexico to what he described as the Republicans’ “perceived loss” in the midterm elections.

double quotation markHuge CARAVANS are forming and beginning their illegal march through Mexico. Many of the people in these Caravans are those that various countries don’t want - “Send them to America,” they say - But they will not be accepted! MEXICO MUST STOP THEM, NOW, and if they do not do so, the Tariffs on Mexico will be IMMEDIATELY DOUBLED. MEXICO, THE GOVERNOR OF TEXAS, THE VERY LIBERAL NEW GOVERNOR OF TEXAS, OUR GREAT BORDER PATROL, & ICE, HAVE BEEN SO INFORMED. There will be no leniency!

The threat came as approximately 1,500 people, many travelling with children, began walking north from Tapachula in southern Mexico on Tuesday following the Democrats’ midterm victory, according to Reuters.

Donald Trump has been busy posting his latest commentary on Truth Social this morning, publishing a series of posts in which he takes aim at Democrats, revisits old grievances and accuses his political opponents of corruption.

In one post, the US president launched an attack on the Democratic party, describing its leadership as “one of the most corrupt and anti-American” in the country’s history. Coming just days after the Republicans suffered significant losses in the midterm elections, Trump’s latest broadside against Democrats appears to be an attempt to rally his party, as he urges Republicans to “fight hard”.

double quotation markThe Democrat Party, lead by one of the most Corrupt and anti-American groups of political leaders and hacks in the history of our Country, and even the World, is doing everything in their power to get away from MASSIVE BLUE STATE CORRUPTION by saying, over and over again, that the Trump Administration is corrupt. It is a sound bite that they viciously use, over and over again, in order to nullify the TREMENDOUS & UNPRECEDENTED theft that has taken place in our Blue States - Minnesota, California, and others, all over the U.S.A.

In a subsequent post, Trump returned to the controversy surrounding his personal tax returns during his first presidential term. He recalled what he described as a “relentless effort” by Democrats to obtain his tax records, claiming that, after the matter reached the Supreme Court, accountants spent a year examining his finances in an effort to find wrongdoing.

Unlike previous presidents in recent decades, Trump refused to voluntarily release his returns while campaigning for the White House and throughout his first term. After a lengthy legal battle, six years of Trump’s tax returns, covering 2015 to 2020, were subsequently made public by the House ways and means committee. You can read more on that here.

double quotation markNow, in order to deflect from MASSIVE BLUE STATE CORRUPTION & CRIME, they are at it again, illegally threatening Republicans with knowingly false accusations and charges. Other than cheating, this is how they won the Midterms - But we won’t let our Country go to hell!

title: 'No light, no water, no heat': Ukrainians struggle with blackouts as Russia hits power grid
excerpt:
Single mother Daryna Kulchytska has been trying to giver her son Kyryll (left) and daughter Olena (right) as normal a childhood as possible

Daryna Kulchytska is a mum under pressure. A single parent ...
body_text:
Single mother Daryna Kulchytska has been trying to giver her son Kyryll (left) and daughter Olena (right) as normal a childhood as possible

Daryna Kulchytska is a mum under pressure. A single parent in a seventh floor flat in Kyiv trying to feed two lively kids and ensure they do their homework. But Daryna also faces the added strain of a deadline she can't even be certain of.

All she knows is soon the lights will go out, the sockets will lose power, the wi-fi will drop, and the taps will run dry. Tonight, the electricity has kept flowing an hour longer than advertised, but Daryna's still racing to serve dinner and finish her own work from home.

"The last few days it was only four or five hours we had power, but it's not at the same times. For two hours we have electricity, then for eight hours we don't."

As peace talks continue, with US envoys meeting the Russian and Ukrainian leaders on Thursday, Ukrainians are facing a rolling schedule of planned power cuts because of intensified Russian attacks on their energy grid. Ukraine has responded by striking Russian oil refineries.

Officials are concerned that life will quickly become unsustainable for millions of Ukrainians if power supplies cannot be maintained for at least four hours per day. Some privately warn that's close already, as some families are living with outages of up to 20 hours in Kyiv.

The power cuts were introduced earlier this year than last winter, and they're already lasting longer - making homes like Daryna's darker and colder. She's wrapped in layers of clothing and a heavy coat - the temperature is dropping, indoors and out.

Just before 7:30pm, there's a click and that's it - darkness until dawn.

The lift doesn't work, the water will stop flowing because electricity is needed to pump it to their flat. So the torches and LED candles come out and Daryna, her son Kyryll and daughter Olena gather for a card game of Uno before an early night.

Twelve-year-old Kyryll, speaking perfect English learned during two years living in the US, is frank about the disruption.

"There's no light, no water, no heat, no electricity. And no fun. All the fun got sucked out with the electricity," he says. "We have a lot of board games. We have a whole shelf, but we've played them like a hundred thousand times already."

Many families sit in the shadows as blackouts sweep entire neighbourhoods, smothering homes and streets in darkness.

"You look outside and sometimes you see nothing. You have a big city around but you see nothing because there's no light," Daryna says.

Kyiv has been worst hit - its metro trains and trolleybuses at times brought to a standstill. Nationwide, hundreds of thousands of Ukrainians have gone without power in recent weeks.

We saw why on a visit to one of Ukraine's largest power stations, barely standing after a recent ballistic missile strike - the most powerful and devastating attack of Russia's campaign against Ukrainian energy targets.

Damaged parts from the power plant lie scattered on the ground

The enormous plant - which we've been asked not to name for security reasons - has been reduced to a pile of twisted metal and broken pipes, its turbines buried in rubble, taking the site completely off line.

Volodymyr Kovalenko was on duty in the control room keeping the plant working when the missiles hit at 3am.

"It was a very powerful attack. We'd never experienced anything like it. We'd had strikes before – part of the roof had collapsed, it was pretty grim. But this time it was particularly severe."

Kovalenko, who followed in his parents' footsteps and has worked at the site for 25 years, says the damage is heartbreaking, though he's confident it can be repaired.

But the work is being hampered by air raids every 15-30 minutes – seven times during our four-hour visit. Each warning of drones and further missiles forces teams to down tools and dive for cover, though during our visit all were shot down or flew on towards other targets.

If there isn't time to reach the site's main shelter, the workers hide in the foundations of its towering chimneys.

"It's very difficult," says Vadym Bobyr, who is leading the recovery effort. "You've mentally prepared yourself to do a particular job, and then… the air raid siren goes off, and you have to get out as quickly as possible."

The 39-year-old, who has worked here half his life, is dwarfed by the mangled ruins and daunted by the challenge of rebuilding the plant.

"It's emotionally difficult, because we've already repaired all this, got it running again, and now it's happened all over again. It hurts, but we keep working and getting things done."

As we speak there's another alert - an incoming Banderol cruise missile.

The workers dart through the maze of passages and pipework but there isn't time to reach a shelter - one of the plant's thickest walls will have to do for cover. The missile was eventually intercepted 5km (3 miles) away.

Energy workers are at enormous risk. Since August there have been almost daily attacks on power facilities, claiming several lives every week. And it's getting more dangerous.

On the edge of the site, with the latest threat over, a team returns to reinstating the power lines feeding the national grid. But they won't be carrying electricity from the shattered plant before the end of this winter, at least.

President Volodymyr Zelensky says Ukraine still has enough generating capacity to meet electricity demand - the problem is getting it to homes and businesses when so many power lines and substations have been hit. Russia is using "waiter drones" that cling to pylons and cables and go undetected until Russia decides to detonate them.

Maxim Timchenko, CEO of DTEK, Ukraine's largest private energy company, said Russia was already putting the degraded electricity grid under even greater pressure than last year, and that overstretched air defences were unable to protect all of Ukraine's critical infrastructure.

"What is different is the scale of attacks and the different types of weapons used in these attacks. This is what is the difference - they've doubled in power and in scale".

He said rebuilding the damaged power station would take at least until next summer, because workers under sustained attack were limited to only one or two productive hours per day.

"We are fighting for survival of not only the whole country but ordinary people, especially during winter," Timchenko says.

Volodymyr Kovalenko has worked at the power station for 25 years

Kovalenko echoes the sense of mission about trying to keep the lights on. "Energy is the foundation of everything - people's lives, the state. Nothing can function without it. I've dedicated my entire life to this".

Many are choosing to leave the capital, or Ukraine altogether, to avoid months of bitter cold. Daryna, Kyryll and Olena know the winter has barely begun.

"It's the worst feeling," Kyryll says. "When I get home from school, I'm tired. I lay in my bed. Bam! Air alarm. Bam! No lights. Bam! A lot of homework. Bam!"

When the children are in bed Daryna confides her thoughts of moving to somewhere safer, or warmer. She's torn by the desire to stay at home - close to friends and relatives - and the worry of how unbearable life may become.

The strain is damaging her mental health, she tells me, and she fears the impact on Kyryll and Olena, who suffers nightmares. Still, Daryna remains defiant despite the darkness.

"I don't want to live without light. But actually people in Ukraine say, OK, without light, but without Russians. Yes, we're scared, we're scared a lot. But better for us to be without power, but [also] without Russians."

Additional reporting by Anastasiia Levchenko, Kamila Hrabchuk and Daniel Wittenberg

title: Israeli strike on Gaza hospital kills six Palestinians, health ministry says
excerpt:
First responders from the Civil Defence inspect the damage at Nasser hospital in Khan Younis

At least six people have been killed and a large number injured in an Israeli air strike on Nasser hospita...
body_text:
First responders from the Civil Defence inspect the damage at Nasser hospital in Khan Younis

At least six people have been killed and a large number injured in an Israeli air strike on Nasser hospital, the biggest hospital in the southern Gaza Strip, the Hamas-run health ministry says.

Eyewitnesses told the BBC that a single missile fired by a warplane hit a building containing the surgical wards and intensive care units overnight.

The health ministry said medical staff, patients and companions were killed. It condemned the attack as a "flagrant violation of international laws and conventions".

The Israeli military said it struck a senior Hamas figure and other operatives from the group's armed wing who had been operating within the hospital.

It alleged that they had violated international law by using the hospital as "a command centre for military and terrorist activities".

Hamas did not comment on the claim. But it accused Israel of killing patients and medical staff and perpetrating "a full-fledged war crime".

Under international law, hospitals have a protected status, but they have been repeatedly targeted during the Gaza war.

Israel accuses Hamas, which retains security control of parts of Gaza not occupied by Israeli troops, of cynically exploiting civilian infrastructure. It says the group stores weapons and runs command and control rooms in hospitals, which Hamas denies.

Israel does not allow international news organisations, including the BBC, into Gaza, making it difficult to verify what is happening in the territory.

In a video posted on social media, a paramedic from the Civil Defence agency who arrived at the building after the strike early on Thursday said the missile penetrated the five-storey structure and hit a room in the surgical department.

A spokesman for the Civil Defence, which operates under the Hamas-run interior ministry, initially said that five people had been killed and 20 others injured.

Videos shared by activists showed thick smoke inside the building and extensive destruction on the second floor, where medical equipment and beds had been scattered by the blast.

Local activists have also circulated claims that the strike may have targeted a senior Hamas security figure who was hiding inside the building.

Speaking to reporters in the aftermath of the strike, the director of Nasser hospital said the building had been hit in a vertical strike, causing extensive damage.

Nasser hospital was hit by a double Israeli strike in August 2025, which killed at least 20 people, including journalists and health workers.

Israeli strikes on Gaza have continued despite a ceasefire agreement in October last year.

More than 1,620 people have been killed since then, according to the territory's health ministry, whose figures are considered reliable by the UN.

Israel and Hamas have accused each other of violating the ceasefire.

The humanitarian crisis in Gaza has recently worsened as a result of heavy rains that reportedly flooded tens of thousands of tents housing displaced families.

The Gaza war was triggered by the Hamas-led attack on southern Israel on 7 October 2023, when about 1,200 people were killed and 251 others were taken hostage.

Since then, more than 74,650 people have been killed in Gaza, the health ministry says.
